title: fix(pulse): worktree cleanup starved by cycle budget after long early dispatch; worktrees pile up
body:
## Summary

Since v3.39.132 (GH#37051 / #37055), `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` is deferred with
"cycle budget exhausted" in most pulse cycles, because `preflight_early_dispatch` uses the cycle
budget first. That stage is the one that starts `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`, so worktree
cleanup runs every 1–4 hours instead of every pulse cycle, and worktrees accumulate on disk.
Same starvation pattern as #33246, for a different stage: #33247 fixed that one with a catch-up in
the async post-dispatch housekeeping lane (`blocker_refresh_catchup`, run with
`AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_CYCLE_CLAMP=0`); worktree cleanup has no such path.

## Environment

- aidevops v3.39.135 (v3.39.132 installed 2026-11-07 15:22 UTC), auto-updated
- NixOS 26.05, x86_64, shared workstation, 4 workers, repos `awardsapp/awardsapp` and
  `marcusquinn/aidevops`

## What happens

`_run_preflight_stages` (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) runs early dispatch, then cleanup:

```bash
_pulse_run_budget_priority_stage "preflight_early_dispatch" _preflight_early_dispatch || _pflt_ed_rc=$?
...
run_stage_with_timeout "preflight_cleanup_and_ledger" "$_pflt_timeout" \
	_preflight_cleanup_and_ledger || true
```

`_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout` (`pulse-watchdog.sh`) now subtracts the main dispatch reserve from
the remaining cycle time (GH#37051) and defers the stage when less than 15 s remain:

```bash
if [[ "$remaining" -lt 15 ]]; then
	echo "[pulse-wrapper] Stage deferred: ${stage_name} cycle budget exhausted" >>"$LOGFILE"
	return 124
fi
```

`preflight_early_dispatch` currently takes 400–1190 s. After such a run the next stage in
`pulse-stage-timings.log` is `preflight_post_label_refill`; the cleanup stages are absent. When
early dispatch takes 0–45 s, `cleanup_orphans` … `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` run and the async
worktree cleanup starts.

## Evidence

`pulse-stage-timings.log`, 2026-11-08:

| Stage | Runs | Avg | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preflight_early_dispatch` | 51 | 662 s | 1192 s |
| `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` | 11 | 16 s | 17 s |

`pulse.log`: `Stage deferred: preflight_cleanup_and_ledger cycle budget exhausted` × 65,
`Stage complete: preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` × 111.

The pulse itself is not slower (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`):

| Day | Cycles | Avg duration |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-06 | 61 | 1322 s |
| 2026-11-07 | 74 | 1072 s |
| 2026-11-08 | 55 | 932 s |

Worktree cleanup (`cleanup_worktrees.log`, `[cleanup-worktrees-async]` starts / completed runs /
worktrees removed):

| Day | Started | Completed | Removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-05 | 29 | 25 | 107 |
| 2026-11-06 | 57 | 50 | 120 |
| 2026-11-07 | 38 | 32 | 62 |
| 2026-11-08 | 12 | 7 | 4 |

Completed runs on 2026-11-07/08: every 20–40 min until ~11:20 UTC, then 12:42, 14:01, 16:07,
17:07, 18:22, 18:57, 20:12, 20:35, 00:19, 02:13, 04:30, 05:31, 07:21, 11:24, 15:24. The gaps
began before v3.39.132 was installed (long early dispatch alone), and grew after it.

Result: 63 directories in the worktree base directory (49 created on 2026-11-07/08), 81 GB, most of them
4.8 GB `awardsapp` worktrees; the user's disk quota is nearly full. The only other path that starts
the helper, `_dispatch_launch_pressure_cleanup`, fires rarely and removes 1–3 per run.

Not verified by experiment: that GH#37051 is the main cause, rather than early dispatch getting
longer. The deferral and its correlation with early dispatch duration are from the logs above.

## Expected

Worktree cleanup starts every cycle (subject to its own cadence gate,
`CLEANUP_WORKTREES_ASYNC_CADENCE_MIN`), whatever early dispatch costs. Starting it is cheap: it
is already async (transient user service or `setsid nohup`) and returns immediately.

## Possible fixes

- As in #33247: a worktree-cleanup catch-up in `_pulse_run_post_dispatch_housekeeping_stages`
  (`pulse-dispatch-engine-housekeeping.sh`) when `cleanup_worktrees.last-run` is older than the
  cadence. Note that this lane is itself often incomplete here: `pulse.log` shows `Async
  post-dispatch housekeeping: started` × 172 and `incomplete — preserving successful stages for
  resume` × 143 (`dedup_cleanup`, `auto_decomposer_scanner`, `fast_fail_prune_expired` deferred);
  not investigated further.
- Launch `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` (and the stash helper) outside the budgeted
  `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` stage, e.g. at the start of `_run_preflight_stages`, as
  `_preflight_start_merge_first` does for the merge routine.
- Or exempt the async launch from `_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout`, since it does not consume the
  cycle budget.
- A test like `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`: early dispatch that consumes the whole budget
  must still launch the worktree cleanup helper.


### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-systemd-unit-generation.sh`

title: bug(pulse-todo-sync): handoff PR never created — body has no standalone For #N line
body:
## Summary

The pulse planning-sync protected-branch handoff pushes its branch successfully, then fails to
open the handoff PR because the generated body contains no standalone `For #N` line. The
`origin:worker` identity guard rejects the create, so protected-branch publication is deferred on
every cycle and never converges. Each cycle leaves another orphan branch on the remote.

Observed on `marcusquinn/aidevops`: **95 abandoned `aidevops/pulse-todo-*` branches** on the
public remote, and `status=protected_branch_publication_deferred ... wake=handoff_recovery`
repeating every pulse cycle.

## Evidence

Wrapper log for a single cycle — push succeeds, PR creation is refused, publication defers:

```
remote: Create a pull request for 'aidevops/pulse-todo-b3097bfa5c0a942a' on GitHub by visiting:
remote:      https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/new/aidevops/pulse-todo-b3097bfa5c0a942a
[OK] Published allowlisted files (1a5795f5e9533f610df158dca93ca12529488db7)
[SAFETY] worker PR body has ambiguous or missing explicit issue identity; keep one standalone `For #N` line; move other references under `## Related`.
[pulse-wrapper] ... status=protected_branch_publication_deferred repo=marcusquinn/aidevops wake=handoff_recovery
```

(The elided prefix in the last line is the stage's own `ref sync` label.)

The body generator at `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh:111-116` emits exactly three
parts: an HTML comment marker, a publication prose section, and a `## Related issues` list. The
issue number is used only in the **title** (`.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh:124`),
which the guard never reads.

The guard inspects the body only (`.agents/scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh:262-275`). Its
extractor skips HTML comments (`:182-183`) and skips everything under a heading matching
`related` (`:190,:193`), which `## Related issues` does match. Nothing carrying an issue reference
survives in the primary section, so `issues` is empty and the create is rejected at `:270-274`.

The identity value already exists in scope: `issue_num` is computed at
`.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh:95` from the handoff linkage and is already the
identity used by the title.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -c 'status=protected_branch_publication_deferred' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log`

**Actual output:**

```
157
```

One deferral per pulse cycle, with no handoff PR created in any of them.

**Symptom command:** `git ls-remote --heads https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops.git 'refs/heads/aidevops/pulse-todo-*' | wc -l`

**Actual output:**

```
95
```

**Expected output:** one pending handoff PR per distinct handoff id, and no growth in abandoned
`aidevops/pulse-todo-*` branches.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh:110-116` — emit one standalone `For #${issue_num}`
  line in the primary body section, above `## Related issues`, so the existing identity is visible
  to the guard. Keep the linkage list under its current heading so it stays excluded as secondary.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh:95` — `issue_num` can be empty when the linkage has no
  `#N` (the `grep | sed` pipeline exits through `sed`, which succeeds on empty input). Guard it:
  an empty identity must fail the handoff explicitly rather than produce `GH#:` in the title and a
  bare `For #` in the body.

Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/gh-closing-reference-lib.sh:190` defines which headings are
treated as secondary; the primary section is everything not under `remaining`, `follow-up`,
`related` or `next steps`. A planning handoff references many issues and closes none, so a
non-closing `For #N` is the correct declaration — not `Resolves`.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh` must pass; it already asserts the
  deferred-status path at `:391-393`.
- Add a case asserting the generated handoff body yields exactly one explicit issue through
  `_gh_pr_body_explicit_issues`, and that an empty `issue_num` fails the handoff instead of
  emitting a malformed title or body.
- `shellcheck` clean on the modified script.
- Cleaning up the existing 95 abandoned remote branches is a separate operational decision; do not
  delete remote refs as part of this fix.

## Notes

Two further consequences of the same stall, both worth tracking separately rather than widening
this fix:

- Each deferred cycle creates and discards a full workspace clone, feeding the recovery-bucket
  growth in #37214.
- `run_stage_with_timeout` logs the documented non-failure deferral codes (`4` handoff pending,
  `24`/`25` snapshot classes) as `Stage failed: sync_todo_refs_repo_N exited with N`, and
  `batch completed ... failures=2` counts a legitimate deferral as a failure. The resulting log
  reads as a hard failure for what the code treats as an expected wait state.

title: bug(tests): hardcoded /usr/bin/git makes 65 scripts unrunnable on non-FHS hosts
body:
## Summary

65 files under `.agents/scripts` invoke Git through the hardcoded absolute path `/usr/bin/git`.
That path does not exist on NixOS (and is absent on any non-FHS or Nix-managed host), so every
affected test aborts with exit 127 before running a single assertion. Required repository gates are
therefore unrunnable on such hosts, which blocks delivery rather than reporting a test failure.

This is the probable root of the largest recorded worker blocker cluster on this installation:
a single `runner_capability_unmet` fingerprint with **95 attempts** on one private repo and
**71 attempts** on `marcusquinn/aidevops`, across roughly 100 issues. Those blocker details
repeatedly cite `spawn git ENOENT` and "Git unavailable in the synthetic test's fixed, sanitized
PATH".

## Reproducer

Live reproduction while verifying an unrelated change on a NixOS host:

**Symptom command:** `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh`

**Actual output:**

```
.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh: line 19: /usr/bin/git: No such file or directory
```

Exit status 127. The harness never reaches its assertions.

The shim responsible (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh:13-21`):

```bash
export PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:${PATH}"

# Fixture repositories are intentionally isolated under TMP. Use native Git so
# the production canonical-worktree shim does not classify them as service
# mirrors during local verification.
git() {
	/usr/bin/git "$@"
	return $?
}
```

The intent is correct and must be preserved: the test needs **native** Git so the production
canonical-worktree wrapper does not treat fixture repositories as service mirrors. Only the
hardcoded FHS path is wrong.

Host facts:

**Symptom command:** `ls /usr/bin/git; command -v git; command -v -p git`

**Actual output:**

```
ls: cannot access '/usr/bin/git': No such file or directory
~/.aidevops/bin/git
/run/current-system/sw/bin/git
```

`command -v git` resolves to the aidevops wrapper, which is exactly what these tests are avoiding.
`command -v -p git` searches the default system PATH and resolves native Git on both FHS and
non-FHS hosts, so it satisfies the original intent portably.

Scope:

**Symptom command:** `rg -l '/usr/bin/git' .agents/scripts | wc -l`

**Actual output:**

```
65
```

The test above alone contains 24 occurrences.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh:13-21` and the remaining 64 files listed by
  `rg -l '/usr/bin/git' .agents/scripts` — resolve native Git once into a variable and call that,
  instead of hardcoding the path. `command -v -p git` is the portable equivalent of the current
  intent; fail closed with a clear message when it resolves to nothing.
- Prefer a single shared helper over 65 independent edits: the existing shared test scaffolding is
  the natural owner, so a resolver such as `test_native_git` can be defined once and sourced. Keep
  the per-file `git()` shim shape so call sites stay unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/install-hooks.sh` and `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh` also hardcode the
  path and are not tests; treat their fix as production-affecting and verify separately.

Reference pattern: the existing comment at `:15-17` states the requirement (native Git, not the
wrapper). Any replacement must keep bypassing `~/.aidevops/bin/git` while resolving correctly
where Git lives outside `/usr/bin`.

## Verification

- On a non-FHS host, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-project-root.sh` must reach its
  assertions instead of exiting 127.
- On an FHS host the resolved path must remain native Git, and fixture repositories must still not
  be classified as service mirrors — the behaviour the shim exists to guarantee.
- Add a focused case asserting the resolver never returns the aidevops wrapper path, so a future
  change cannot silently route fixtures through the production shim.
- `shellcheck` clean on every modified script.

## Notes

The failure mode is worse than an ordinary red test: exit 127 arrives before any assertion, so an
affected runner cannot distinguish "environment lacks a path" from "change is broken". Several of
the historical blocker reports show workers correctly preserving their implementation and declining
to push, having concluded the repository gate could not pass — the implementations were sound and
the gate was unrunnable.

Platform support policy lives in `reference/platform-support.md`; if non-FHS hosts are outside the
supported matrix, the gate should state that explicitly and skip with a documented reason rather
than failing with a missing-file error.

title: bug(opencode-db-archive): archived event expiry unreachable behind active-DB preflight, archive events grow unbounded
body:
## Summary

Archived OpenCode event rows grow without bound on any workstation that is actually in use. The
only mechanism that can expire them, `archive --archive-event-retention-days N`, is unreachable:
it is gated behind an active-DB idle preflight that a live OpenCode session always fails, and no
caller passes the flag anyway because its default is 0 (disabled).

Measured on one installation, events are 85% of the archive database:

| Database | Size | Events | Event bytes | Sessions |
|----------|------|--------|-------------|----------|
| `opencode-archive.db` | 22.1 GB | 1,759,890 | **18.7 GB** | 2,494 |
| `opencode.db` | 4.4 GB | 500,263 | **3.6 GB** | 591 |

All 2,494 archived sessions were inactive for more than 7 days (0 updated in the last 7 days), so
every archived event row was already eligible for expiry under a 7-day policy and none of it could
ever be removed.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `opencode-db-archive.sh archive --archive-event-retention-days 7 --dry-run --max-duration-seconds 120`

**Actual output:**

```
[WARN] Archive deferred — 4 process(es) hold the active DB open (holder PID <pid> has 1 busy session(s)).
```

**Expected:** archived event expiry targets only the archive DB, which was completely idle at that
moment (`opencode-archive.db-wal` was 0 bytes, `freelist_count` 0). It should proceed, or defer for
a reason that concerns the archive DB.

The deferral comes from `_archive_mutation_preflight` (`opencode-db-archive.sh:249-267`), which
checks `_db_holder_count "$ACTIVE_DB"`, active WAL stability and the **active** schema, then
returns 2 and aborts the whole command. `_archive_expire_events` is only reached later, at
`opencode-db-archive.sh:1277`, well after that gate:

```bash
_archive_mutation_preflight() {
	holder_count=$(_db_holder_count "$ACTIVE_DB")
	...
	if [[ "$holder_count" -gt 0 ]] && ! _archive_enter_held_mode "$holder_count"; then
		return 2
	fi
```

The held-mode escape hatch cannot help: `opencode_db_idle_gate` rejects any busy holder
(`:270-287`), and the session running the command is itself a busy holder. So the operation is
structurally impossible during interactive use, which is precisely when sessions accumulate.

The statement that would do the work only touches `$ARCHIVE_DB` (`:1107`):

```sql
DELETE FROM event WHERE rowid IN (SELECT e.rowid FROM event e JOIN session s ON s.id=e.aggregate_id WHERE s.time_updated < $cutoff LIMIT $ARCHIVE_BATCH_SIZE);
```

It reads and writes nothing in the active DB, so the active-DB preflight is not protecting it.

Second, nothing ever requests it:

**Symptom command:** `rg -l 'archive-event-retention-days|ARCHIVE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS' .agents`

**Actual output:**

```
.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh
```

Only the implementation and its own test. Scheduled hygiene wires up a different and much blunter
mechanism: `storage-cleanup-helper.sh:223-232` previews only the `prune` path, gated behind
`storage.opencode_session_retention_days`, which defaults to 0 and whose effect is **permanent
deletion of whole sessions**. So the shipped choice is "keep 18.7 GB of raw events forever" or
"destroy 2,494 sessions of conversation history", with no option to drop just the low-value event
stream.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh:1277` and `:249-267` — run `_archive_expire_events`
  before, or independently of, `_archive_mutation_preflight`. It mutates only `$ARCHIVE_DB`, so
  gate it on archive-DB holders and archive WAL stability, not the active DB's. Keep the existing
  active-DB preflight for the session-moving phase that genuinely needs it.
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive.sh:1128` — `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS` defaults
  to 0. A disabled-by-default retention on append-only event data guarantees unbounded growth;
  consider defaulting it to the worker retention window (7 days) for the archive DB only.
- `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh:223-232` — scheduled hygiene should request archived
  event expiry, which preserves conversations, in preference to session pruning. Report reclaimable
  event bytes in the preview so the operator sees the cheap option first.
- Consider the same expiry for active-DB event rows belonging to sessions already archived.

Reference pattern: `_archive_expire_events` already batches with `.timeout` and honours
`--max-duration-seconds`, so it is safe to run against a held DB in small batches; that is the
design the held-mode path uses for session moves.

## Verification

- With a busy holder on the active DB, `archive --archive-event-retention-days 7 --apply` must
  expire eligible archive event rows and report the count, instead of deferring.
- `session`, `message`, `part` and `todo` counts in the archive DB must be unchanged by event
  expiry; only `event` rows may disappear. `PRAGMA quick_check` must stay `ok`.
- `stats` must show the reclaimed event bytes, and repeated runs must be idempotent (second run
  expires 0 rows).
- Add a case to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh` asserting event expiry proceeds
  while the active DB is held, since that is the regression being fixed.

## Notes

Because `auto_vacuum` is 0, expiry returns pages to the freelist rather than shrinking the file:
growth stops immediately and the space is reused, with an actual size reduction only after a later
VACUUM. That is the desired behaviour for quota control and worth stating in the preview output, so
an operator does not conclude the run did nothing when the file size is unchanged.

This is the root cause of the disk-usage growth investigated in #37214 and the reason an
installation can reach tens of GB of session storage while reporting only a few hundred MB of
active conversation data.

title: review-issue-pr: adding a type label (bug) after approval permanently stales the signed approval
body:
## What happened

During an interactive `/review-issue-pr` session, an issue's signed approval verified (`APPROVAL_REASON: proven-locked-continuity`). The reviewer then applied the labels the review recommended (`bug`, `tier:simple`) with `gh issue edit --add-label`. `approval-helper.sh verify issue` then returned `STALE_APPROVAL` (`stale-or-unproven-continuity`). Removing the labels again did not restore it, so the maintainer had to sign a second time.

## Cause

`.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`, `_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity()`, replays every lifecycle event after the approval comment. Its case statement (around line 345) accepts only assignment, status, tier, `auto-dispatch`, `needs-maintainer-review` and `fix-the-fixer` label events; anything else hits `*) return 1`. A `labeled:bug` event stays in the timeline permanently, so the approval cannot recover.

The review workflow points reviewers to this path. `workflows/review-issue-pr.md` → Review Output Format has a `**Labels**: [e.g., tier:simple, bug, status:available]` line under the recommendation, but never says that non-lifecycle labels must be applied before the maintainer signs.

Adding `tier:standard` alone after approval is fine (allowed and verified on a sibling issue). Only type labels (`bug`, `enhancement`, …) break the approval.

## Fix (choose one, the first is smaller)

1. `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md`, Approval sequencing: require the reviewer to apply every recommended non-lifecycle label (type labels such as `bug` / `enhancement`) **before** presenting the `sudo aidevops approve` command, and to apply only lifecycle/tier labels afterwards. Mirror the rule in the `**Labels**` line of the output template.
2. Alternatively, decide whether type labels by an admin/maintain/write actor are non-scope-bearing, and if so add them to the allowlist in `_approval_continuity_lifecycle_change_allowed()` and the replay case statement (trust-boundary change: needs its own review).

## Verification

- Option 1: read the updated workflow, then on a test issue apply `bug` before approval, sign, add `tier:simple` afterwards, and `approval-helper.sh verify issue N owner/repo` returns `VERIFIED`.
- Option 2: same sequence with `bug` added after approval returns `VERIFIED`; an unauthorized actor's label event still returns `STALE_APPROVAL`.

title: issue-triage-gate: private org members with write access are gated as external (CONTRIBUTOR skips the permission lookup)
body:
## What happened

A repository admin opened an issue in an organisation repository. The Issue Triage Gate labelled it `external-contributor` and `needs-maintainer-review`, removed `status:available`, and posted the external welcome comment. The maintainer then had to review and cryptographically approve their own issue.

Run log: `Author <admin> has role CONTRIBUTOR — applying triage gate`.

Evidence:

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{user}/permission` → `admin`.
- `GET /orgs/{org}/public_members` → `[]` (the admin's org membership is private).
- An authenticated `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}` as that member reports `author_association: MEMBER`, but the `issues` webhook payload reported `CONTRIBUTOR`. GitHub hides private org membership in event payloads.

## Cause

`.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate-reusable.yml` (github-script step) trusts `OWNER`/`MEMBER` from `issue.author_association`, and runs the live `collaborators/{username}/permission` lookup only when the association is `COLLABORATOR`. A private org member with admin/maintain/write access arrives as `CONTRIBUTOR` (or `NONE` before their first contribution), so the lookup is skipped and they are gated as external.

## Fix

In the reusable workflow, run the existing live permission lookup for every association that is not already trusted (at least `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIMER`, `NONE`), not only `COLLABORATOR`. Keep the current fail-closed `catch` (treat as untrusted on lookup errors), the `external-contributor`-label override and the bot handling unchanged. After the change, re-pin the caller SHA in managed repos (`aidevops sync-workflows --workflow issue-triage-gate`).

Workaround until then: make the org membership public.

## Verification

- An admin whose org membership is private opens an issue in a managed org repo: the log shows the permission lookup and `bypassing triage`, and no `external-contributor` / `needs-maintainer-review` labels are added.
- A user with read access only, or none, opening an issue is still gated.

title: Background gh auth token calls open a macOS keychain dialog every cycle when the login keychain is locked or reset
body:
## What happened

On a macOS 26 host, the login keychain could not be unlocked at login. macOS set it aside as `login_renamed_1.keychain-db` and created an empty replacement. For the next ~5 hours a "security wants to use the keychain" dialog reappeared about every 16 seconds. It looked like an unknown process asking for secrets, which slowed a security investigation.

Process ancestry captured while the dialog was showing:

```
launchd (sh.aidevops.pulse-merge-routine, every 120s)
  -> pulse-merge-routine.sh run
    -> github_auth_runtime.py exec-gh
      -> gh auth token --hostname github.com
        -> /usr/bin/security find-generic-password -s gh:github.com -wa <user>
          -> SecurityAgent GUI prompt
```

`_pmr_require_gh_auth()` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh:309`) calls `gh auth token` with no check on whether the keychain can answer without user interaction. gh's keyring backend runs `/usr/bin/security`. When the item is missing or the keychain is locked, that call opens a GUI dialog instead of failing fast. Each launchd tick, and every other caller of `gh auth token`, opens a new dialog.

Related symptom with an unconfirmed caller: TCC logs showed `org.gpgtools.pinentry-mac` being activated about once a minute from 14:00 to 14:40 UTC while the GnuPG passphrase item was missing from the replacement keychain. This is probably a `gopass`/GPG read from a background routine. A worker should confirm the caller before changing it.

Related closed issues covering different paths: #34511, #33904.

## Proposed fix

1. Add a shared non-interactive keychain readiness check for macOS background routines.
   - It must not prompt. Example: `SecKeychainGetStatus` on the default keychain via `python3` ctypes, returning "unlocked" only when `kSecUnlockStateStatus` is set.
   - Alternative: run `/usr/bin/security` with user interaction disabled, if a CLI-safe method exists.
   - Non-macOS hosts must always pass the check.
2. Call the check before `gh auth token` in background contexts:
   - `_pmr_require_gh_auth()` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh`
   - `.agents/scripts/worker-token-helper.sh`
   - `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`
   - any other launchd-invoked caller found with `rg -n 'gh auth token' .agents/scripts`
3. When the keychain is locked or the item is missing, log one WARN line and skip the cycle. Back off: keep one marker file and re-check at most every 10 minutes. Never open a GUI dialog from a launchd context.
4. Apply the same guard to background `gopass`/GPG secret reads once the caller is confirmed.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh` (`_pmr_require_gh_auth`)
- `.agents/scripts/worker-token-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`
- New or existing shared helper in `.agents/scripts/` for the readiness check. Source it the same way `shared-constants.sh` is sourced.

## Verification

1. On macOS, run `security lock-keychain ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db`, then `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh run`.
   - Expected: exit without API access, one WARN line in the routine log, and no `SecurityAgent` process (`pgrep -x SecurityAgent` prints nothing).
2. Unlock the keychain and run the routine again. Expected: it proceeds normally.
3. Run ShellCheck on the changed scripts and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`.

title: t18883: aidevops agent type in the buzz-aidevops plugin for Buzz 0.7 previews
body:
## Goal

Add an **aidevops** agent type to the external Buzz plugin `sh.aidevops.buzz` (`.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/`). It runs aidevops agents (OpenCode with the aidevops runtime and Claude models from the OAuth pool) in official Buzz 0.7 preview builds, with the existing per-computer names (`<agent>-<LocalHostName>`, e.g. `aidevops-marcus-macbook-pro-01`).

Why now: the Buzz 0.7 previews ship no OpenCode harness. block/buzz-app#2432 is unmerged, and its design review says new behaviour ships as external plugins after the 10 November launch. The owner chose this route on 2026-11-08 (decision recorded in the t18883 brief).

For #36976 (t18883).

## Upstream API (buzz-app `5d9d1ef33c`, the `v0.7.0-preview.254.1` source)

- `ctx.agents.register({ id, title, description, defaults, run, runOnce, sessions?, sessionControls?, models?, timeoutMs })`. Typed in the author package (`src/plugins/author.ts`, `src/plugins/author.test.mjs:87`), not yet in `docs/plugin-authoring-guide.md` (asked on block/buzz-app#2432).
- `ctx.agents.harness` (`src/features/agent-harness/kit.ts:67-117`), described there as "for a harness a plugin brings":
  - `conversation(delivery, scope)` is undefined unless the owner sent or attested the mention. This replaces our `BUZZ_ACP_RESPOND_TO=owner-only` gate.
  - `systemPrompt(delivery, { scope, cwd, instructions })`
  - `turnPrompt(delivery, conversation, { cursor })` → `{ text, cursor, restore }`
  - `tools(agent, conversation)` → `McpHandler`, served with `ctx.host.serveMcp` (`manifest.host.mcp: true`)
  - `reply(agent, conversation, text)`. This replaces `team-interface-acp-cwd-proxy.mjs` reply routing and the parsing behind #37096 / #37102.
- `ctx.host.spawn(id, { args, cwd, env, onStdout, onStderr })` → `{ write, end, kill, exited }` for a `manifest.host.processes` entry. Program names must be bare names on PATH, no paths (`docs/plugin-authoring-guide.md:103`).
- Reference implementation: block/buzz-app#2432 `src/bundled/opencode/runtime.ts` at `613296ff9` (Apache-2.0). It runs one `opencode acp` process and opens an ACP session per conversation with `mcpServers` from `serveMcp`. Follow the pattern; do not copy its app-internal imports (`ownerReads`, relay, `repositoriesContext`), which installed plugins don't get.

## Approach

1. **Launcher: `aidevops buzz acp`** in `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh`, a Buzz 0.7 variant of the runtime anchor's `aidevops-buzz-acp-interactive`:
   - Reuse `team-interface-buzz-runtime.py prepare`, `team-interface-buzz-worktree.sh resolve`, `team-interface-opencode-overlay.mjs generate` and `opencode-launcher-helper.sh remote-interactive`.
   - Drop the 0.5 `buzz` CLI reply path and the `BUZZ_ACP_*` env checks. Buzz's kit now owns gating, tools and replies. (As built: the cwd proxy stays, in a new `--no-publish` mode, only to bind each session to the agent worktree; `prepare-desktop` is a new `team-interface-buzz-runtime.py` subcommand.)
   - Take `--member <agent>-<host>` and `--project <root>` (absolute, or `~/…`) from the plugin. Validate the member against the roster and this computer's host slug, and the project against registered roots.
   - Must not run `setup.sh` or auto-update (keep the #37074 isolated-session guard).
2. **Plugin agent type** in `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js` (still one ES module, no imports):
   - Manifest: `host.processes: [{ id: "acp", program: "aidevops", args: ["buzz", "acp"] }]` and `host.mcp: true`.
   - A minimal ACP client: `initialize`, `session/new` (with `cwd` and `mcpServers` from `serveMcp`), `session/prompt`, `session/update` streaming, `session/cancel`. Deny `session/request_permission` by default unless the permission profile allows the action.
   - One process per agent. Sessions keyed by `HarnessConversation.key`. (As built: sessions and cursors are kept in memory while the process runs; after a restart the next turn opens a new session shown the conversation so far.)
   - `run(delivery)`: `conversation` → `turnPrompt` → prompt the session → let the agent post through the Buzz tools. If the turn ends with no post, call `harness.reply` with the final text.
   - Config: aidevops agent (roster id, default `aidevops`), project root, scope (`thread`). The display name is computed by the helper from `LocalHostName`.
3. **Docs**: README install and "create an aidevops agent" steps. Update `todo/tasks/t18883-brief.md` to record the reversed "own harness" decision.

title: Detect macOS user-lookup outage (id -un returns a number) and tell the user to restart instead of polling for hours
body:
## What happened

On a macOS 26 host with 23.5 days of uptime (about 980 processes, load average about 16), macOS stopped resolving the logged-in user from about 06:15 UTC. This lasted until a forced restart about 6.5 hours later. Evidence from OpenCode session tool output:

- `id -un` printed `501` instead of the user name (06:20). `dscacheutil -q user -a uid 501` printed nothing (06:21).
- `ssh` and `git commit` failed with `No user exists for uid 501` (06:18–06:20).
- `pgrep` failed with `sysmon request failed with error: sysmond service not found` / `Cannot get process list`, while `sysmond` was still running.
- `dscl . -read` of the user's own record (attribute `UniqueID`) failed with `Operation failed with error: eServerError`. `launchctl print gui/501` failed with `Operation not permitted`.
- `gh` reported offline/unauthenticated and Playwright could not launch Chromium.

Interactive sessions kept polling (`sleep 240; id -un`) for hours, and background routines kept running. The lock screen later rejected the user's correct password, almost certainly for the same reason. The user had to reset the password in Recovery mode, which caused macOS to set the login keychain aside. Only a restart clears this state, and nothing in aidevops told the user that.

## Proposed fix

1. Add a cheap macOS check for broken user lookup to a shared helper.
   - Treat the check as failed when `id -un` prints only digits, or when `dscl . -read` of the current user's record (`UniqueID`) fails.
   - Non-macOS hosts always pass.
2. Pulse and routine pre-flight:
   - When the check fails, skip the cycle and log one WARN line.
   - Write one marker file and send at most one desktop notification per hour: "macOS cannot look up your user account; restart the Mac before entering your password at the lock screen". Use `osascript display notification`, and fail quietly if it can't run.
   - Do not dispatch workers while the check fails.
3. `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1443` sets `runner=$(id -un)`. Guard it so a numeric value is not used as a runner login.
4. Interactive sessions: add a short entry to `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` (or the nearest diagnostics reference). It should say: if `id -un` prints a number or tools report `No user exists for uid`, stop retrying, checkpoint, and tell the user to restart. Warn that the lock screen may reject the correct password while this lasts, and that the user should not reset the password in Recovery mode, because that sets the login keychain aside.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh` or `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (pre-flight gate; confirm which runs first per cycle)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (line ~1443, `runner=$(id -un)`)
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` (diagnostic entry)
- Not yet known: where an OpenCode plugin hook could show the same advisory to interactive sessions. Search `.agents/plugins/` before adding one.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`

## Verification

1. Put a stub `id` first on `PATH` that prints `501` for `-un`, then run one pulse cycle. Expected: no dispatch, one WARN line, one marker file, and no notification on a second run within the hour.
2. Without the stub, the pulse runs as before.

title: terminal-blocker: open input_required circuit on unchanged brief is silently released and redispatched across runners
body:
## Problem

An `input_required` terminal-blocker circuit that waits on a maintainer decision is released on other runners, again and again, though the brief has not changed and no OWNER/MEMBER retry was posted. Each release starts a worker that exits `BLOCKED` within 1–5 minutes. The hold does not last.

## Evidence (public issue in a private managed repo; reference withheld)

- 2026-10-23T22:35Z: runner A posted `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT active=true observations=2 task_revision=8bfe6d8e…`.
- 2026-10-26T06:26Z: a recovery-owner comment names three maintainer dispositions. No maintainer answer since then.
- Issue body: never edited (`lastEditedAt: null`, no `userContentEdits`).
- Label events since 2026-11-07, all without a rearm receipt or retry comment:
  - 11-07T14:47Z available→queued→in-progress (runner B), 14:52Z →blocked
  - 11-07T18:54Z blocked→available (runner A, silent)
  - 11-07T23:54Z dispatch (runner B), 23:56Z →blocked
  - 11-08T16:05Z blocked→available (runner B, silent)
  - 11-08T16:22Z dispatch (runner B), 16:24Z →blocked
- The `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` comments from these three attempts have no `terminal-blocker-observation` marker. The worker exit was probably unclassified, so it fell back to bounded backoff instead of re-joining the open circuit.
- An earlier runner B observation on 2026-11-02 classified the same issue as `runner_capability_unmet` (revision `4ca920a0…`), which projects `status:available`.

## Hypothesis (unverified)

Either (a) unclassified `BLOCKED` exits fall back to bounded backoff, which releases `status:blocked` on expiry without checking for an older open foreign circuit on the same unchanged brief; or (b) `terminal_blocker_task_revision` (`terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:438`) hashes the reason into the revision. A later observation with a different reason then gets a new revision, so the earlier circuit looks re-armed.

## Acceptance

- An open circuit (own or foreign OWNER/MEMBER) on an unchanged brief and dependency set blocks dispatch until there is a brief/dependency revision or a standalone `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`, even when a later attempt was unclassified or used another reason.
- Any automated `status:blocked`→`status:available` transition posts its existing rearm receipt, so the release can be audited.
- Verification: reproduce with fixture issue/comment JSON in the existing terminal-blocker tests, then `shellcheck` the touched scripts.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`

body:
**Task ID:** `t18891` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~1d`
**Logged:** 2026-11-08
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

Session bus chat ingest: scan, verified actor, opt-in owner wakes and redacted listing

## Done when

- [ ] Chat-origin `send`/`ask` text is scanned before it is stored; a blocking verdict refuses the send with exit code 1 and a message naming the reason; a scan error also refuses.
- [ ] `--actor <entity-id>` with a confirmed channel link for that app is framed as verified (and as owner when the entity is the owner); any other actor, or none, is framed as unverified.
- [ ] A chat-origin `ask` wakes an idle session only when the actor is a verified owner and the session opted in with `chat-wake on`; otherwise it waits for the next turn. Rate, pending, hourly-wake and hop limits still apply.
- [ ] `aidevops sessions list --json --redact` omits title, repo, branch, worktree and directory.
- [ ] Regression: session-to-session messages, CLI (non-chat) sends and the outbox behave as before; the existing session-bus tests pass unchanged except where they encoded "chat never wakes".
- [ ] Negative: an `--actor` whose verified link is for a different app or channel ID (for example a SimpleX link used with `chat:matrix:…`) is framed unverified and never wakes; display names in the message text never change the framing.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- **Ingest path:** `sendCommand` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs:81`) builds the chat sender in `chatSender` (`:19-22`) and calls `store.sendMessage` (`session-bus-messages.mjs:104`). Scan and resolve the actor there, before the write. Store the result on the message as `from.trust = { actor, verified, owner, scan }`, and keep `v: 1` readers working by treating a missing `trust` as unverified.
- **Framing:** `senderLabel`/`frameMessage` in `session-bus-format.mjs:70-88` render the chat label. Add the verified/owner state and any scan warning there, and keep the "carries no owner authority" wording for everything except a verified owner.
- **Wake rule:** `isWakeEligible` (`session-bus-delivery.mjs:21-24`) rejects every chat origin. Allow a chat-origin `ask` only when `from.trust.owner === true` and the recipient's opt-in flag is set. Store the opt-in per session under the bus root, for example `chat-wake/<sessionID>.json`, written through a store helper. It must survive restarts and be removed with the session's other files by `prune`.
- **Trust model:** follow `.agents/reference/team-interface-trust.md`: deterministic order at `:38-46`, authority ceilings at `:116-132`, and unknown provenance fails closed at `:141-153`. Entity verification uses `entity-helper.sh verify|link --verified` (usage header `:21-39`). Decide and document how the gateway's channel ID maps to the entity channel (for example `matrix` + `@user:server`).
- **Listing:** `listCommand` (`session-bus-cli-commands.mjs:49`). Add `--redact`, which drops private fields from both the JSON and the text output.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs`: scan, actor resolution, `--actor`, `--redact`, and the `chat-wake` command.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs`: parse the new flags and command.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs`: owner wake rule.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs`: trust framing.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-messages.mjs` or a new `session-bus-chat-trust.mjs`: trust record, scan and opt-in store helpers. Prefer a new module to keep files small.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs`: `chat-wake` action, for the recipient session only.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs`: trust, wake and redaction cases.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/session-bus.md` and `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md`: document the contract.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the plugin delivery path (`session-bus.mjs` tick, `session-bus-delivery.mjs`), the V1 and V2 sidebars (`tui-messages.mjs`), compaction (`session-bus-compaction.mjs`) and `aidevops sessions inbox/outbox` all read message records. Each must tolerate the new optional `from.trust` field.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `sendMessage` and `sendReply` (`session-bus-messages.mjs:104,121`), plus the new opt-in writer.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops` (session-bus suite), `test-team-interface-trust-schema.mjs`.
- **Schemas/config:** message record `v: 1` with an additive optional field. No version bump unless a reader cannot ignore the field.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** a new plugin module must be added to the plugin freshness list in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` (as t18886 did for its modules).
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Old messages lack `trust` and are treated as unverified.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `pruneBus` removes opt-in files for sessions with no presence after retention. Rollback is a code revert; queued messages stay readable.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read `team-interface-trust.md` and `entity-helper.sh verify/link`, and decide the actor-to-entity mapping per app (record it in `reference/session-bus.md`).
2. Add the trust module: scan through `prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-stdin` with a timeout, resolve the actor, and return `{ actor, verified, owner, scan }`, failing closed.
3. Call it from `sendCommand` for chat origins before `sendMessage`. Add `--actor` and `--redact` to the CLI parser.
4. Add the opt-in store (`chat-wake/<sessionID>.json`), the `chat-wake` CLI command and the tool action. Extend `pruneBus` to remove stale opt-ins.
5. Change `isWakeEligible` to allow a chat-origin `ask` only for a verified owner with opt-in, and update the framing.
6. Add unit cases, then run the live self-test under Verification and record the results in the PR.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** write the opt-in and messages with the existing atomic JSON writer (`writeJsonAtomic`). Delivery keeps claiming by rename.
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored data changes; `trust` is additive. Rollback is a code revert, and messages written with `trust` stay readable by the old code.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** an older plugin reading a newer message ignores `trust` and keeps refusing chat wakes, which is safe. A newer plugin treats a message without `trust` as unverified.
- **Idempotency/retry:** re-running `chat-wake on` is a no-op. A gateway retrying a send gets a new message ID; dedupe stays the gateway's job (Matrix already claims events durably).
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a scan that errors or times out refuses the send and never delivers unscanned chat text. An entity lookup failure means unverified. A crash between scan and write leaves nothing behind.
- **Secrets:** never log message text or entity channel IDs at info level.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs`

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-files.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`
- `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`
- `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md`

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs
```

- **Runtime evidence (self-test, no owner needed):** set `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR` to a scratch directory and `XDG_DATA_HOME`/`HOME` overrides for an isolated entity DB if `entity-helper.sh` supports one, else use a scratch entity created and deleted by the test. Start two `opencode serve` sessions with the worktree plugin, following the t18886 live verification in `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md` "Live verification". Then check each of these:
  - An unverified `ask --origin chat:matrix:!room` reaches a busy session framed "unverified" and does not wake an idle one.
  - A text containing a known injection canary from `prompt-guard-helper.sh` tests is refused or flagged.
  - A verified-owner `ask` wakes an idle session only after `chat-wake <session> on`.
  - `list --json --redact` has no title, repo, branch, worktree or directory.
- **Surface mapping:** unit tests cover the trust record, wake rule, opt-in store and redaction. The live run covers CLI ingest, delivery framing and the wake path.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. The changes stay inside the plugin and its docs.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: t18891 chat ingest trust`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no gateway or adapter code (t18893, t18894); no channel bindings or session launch (t18892); no change to session-to-session (non-chat) delivery or limits; the old mailbox stays untouched. Chat messages never get capabilities beyond conversation: no tool or approval authority comes from chat text.

title: t18893: Matrix bot adapter for the session bus: room commands, bound rooms and outbox...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18893` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~6h`
**Logged:** 2026-11-08
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

Matrix bot adapter for the session bus: room commands, bound rooms and outbox relay

**Blocked by:** `t18892`

## Done when

- [ ] With `sessionBus.enabled=true`, `!sessions`, `!ask`, `!send`, `!bind`, `!unbind` and `!launch` map to the matching `aidevops sessions` CLI calls with `--origin chat:matrix:<roomId>` and the resolved `--actor`.
- [ ] In a bound room, `!ai <text>` becomes an `ask` to `channel:matrix:<roomId>`; in an unbound room it uses the existing runner path with no bus call.
- [ ] The relay posts each `outbox/matrix` reply to its room and acknowledges it only after a successful send.
- [ ] `!sessions` in a room with more than two members uses the redacted listing.
- [ ] Regression: with `sessionBus` absent or disabled, the bot behaves exactly as before; the existing Matrix tests pass.
- [ ] Negative: a message whose text starts with `--` or contains newlines and flag-like tokens is passed as text, never as CLI options.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- **New pure module** `.agents/scripts/matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs`: `parseBusCommand(text, prefix)`, `busArgsFor(command, { roomId, actorEntityId })`, and `relayOutbox({ runCli, sendText, now })`. Inject `runCli` (spawn of `aidevops sessions … --json`) and `sendText` so the module needs no network or homeserver in tests.
- **Bot wiring:** in the `room.message` handler (`matrix-bot.mjs.template:383-460`), after `normalizeMatrixIngress` accepts the event and `store.claimEvent` claims it (`:396-398`), check `parseBusCommand` first and route bus commands to the bridge. Keep the per-room `activeDispatches` guard. Entity resolution (`resolveEntityCached`) provides the actor entity ID for `--actor`.
- **Relay timer:** add a relay interval next to the compaction interval (`:373-380`), every 5 s, matching the bus poll. Post with `client.sendText` and acknowledge only after a successful send. Stop it in `shutdown()` (`:501`).
- **Import path:** the generated bot imports helpers from the deployed scripts directory (`matrix-bot.mjs.template:15`, `../../agents/scripts/…`). Use the same path for the bridge.
- **Redaction:** count room members with the SDK (`getJoinedRoomMembers`). Use `aidevops sessions list --json --redact` (t18891) unless the room has exactly two members (the bot and one user).
- **Docs:** add a "Session bus" section to `.agents/services/communications/matrix-bot.md` covering the commands, bound rooms and the owner-only launch.

### Files to Modify

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs`: command parsing, CLI arguments and outbox relay.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/matrix-bot.mjs.template`: route bus commands, relay timer, shutdown.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs`: parser, argument and relay cases with an injected `runCli` and `sendText`, following `test-team-interface-matrix-ingress.mjs`.
- EDIT: `.agents/services/communications/matrix-bot.md`: document the commands.
- EDIT: `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md`: mark the Matrix gateway step.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh` `generate_bot_script` copies the template (`matrix-dispatch-helper.sh:191-193`); the bot process imports the bridge at runtime.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** bus writes happen only through the `aidevops sessions` CLI (`send`, `ask`, `bind`, `unbind`, `launch`, `outbox --ack`); the bot's own `store.claimEvent`/`addMessage` stay as they are.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-matrix-ingress.mjs`, `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-matrix-adapter.mjs`, `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-matrix-session-store.mjs`.
- **Schemas/config:** optional `sessionBus` block in the Matrix bot config (`enabled`, default `false`; `relayIntervalSeconds`, default 5); existing configs keep working.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`; `matrix-dispatch-helper.sh` regenerates the bot from the template on start.
- **Migrations/backfills:** not applicable because the bridge is new-file-only and the config block is optional with a disabled default.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `sessionBus.enabled=false` restores today's behaviour; the relay timer stops in `shutdown()`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Write `matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs` with pure parsing and argument builders, then the relay function with injected I/O.
2. Add the focused test file covering each command, a bound-room `!ai` message, an unbound-room `!ai` message (no bus call), relay success with ack, and relay send failure without ack.
3. Wire the template behind `sessionBus.enabled`, add the relay timer and the shutdown cleanup.
4. Document the commands; run the existing Matrix tests and the new test.
5. Run the scratch-bus check under Verification and record the output in the PR.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the per-room `activeDispatches` guard and the durable `claimEvent` stay in front of bus calls, so a redelivered Matrix event never sends twice. Relay acknowledges only after `sendText` succeeds.
- **Migration/rollback:** disabled by default; turning it off restores the runner-only path.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** a bot running against an older `aidevops` without t18892 gets a CLI error for `bind`/`launch`, which the bridge reports in the room; plain `ask` and `send` still work.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a relay retry after a failed send posts the reply once more at most; ack happens once.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a CLI timeout (10 s) is reported in the room and logged; nothing is acknowledged. A failed `launch` reports the session ID returned by t18892 so the owner can `!bind` it.
- **Trust:** never pass room text as CLI flags. Text goes through `--text-file` or stdin, so a message starting with `--` cannot inject options.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/matrix-bot.mjs.template`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs`
- `.agents/services/communications/matrix-bot.md`
- `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md`

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node .agents/scripts/tests/test-matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs
node .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-matrix-ingress.mjs
node .agents/scripts/tests/test-matrix-session-store.mjs
node --check .agents/scripts/matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs
```

- **Runtime evidence (self-test, no owner needed):** with `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR` set to a scratch directory and one `opencode serve` session (t18886 "Live verification" setup), call the bridge functions from a short Node script using the real `aidevops sessions` CLI as `runCli` and a recording `sendText`. Show that:
  - `!ask` reaches the session and its reply comes back through the relay.
  - The outbox is empty after the ack.
- **Live homeserver check:** a real Synapse or Conduit run is not part of this task. It needs either an existing configured homeserver or the owner's approval for a local container. Record it as a post-merge check in the PR.
- **Surface mapping:** unit tests cover parsing, arguments and relay. The scratch-bus run covers the real CLI and the bus.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. The changes stay in the Matrix bot and its docs.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `node .agents/scripts/tests/test-matrix-session-bus-bridge.mjs`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: t18893 matrix session bus bridge`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no changes to the bus plugin (t18891, t18892 own those); no new homeserver, container or CI job; the unbound-room `!ai` runner path and the session store schema stay unchanged; the old mailbox relay stays untouched.

**AI brief owner:** the interactive owner session of t18886 (marcusquinn).

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

</details>

## Origin

- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** The owner wants to drive OpenCode sessions from mobile chat apps, with one long-running session per channel and per-task sessions launched from chat. They asked for self-testable follow-ups so they are not needed for testing. This is the Matrix gateway from `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md` "Chat-app gateways", built on the trust layer (t18891) and the bindings and launch commands (t18892).

## What

The existing Matrix bot (`matrix-bot.mjs.template`) gains a session-bus bridge:

- **Room commands** for allowlisted users: `!sessions` (redacted list in rooms with more than two members, full list in a direct room), `!ask <target> <text>`, `!send <target> <text>`, `!bind <target>`, `!unbind`, and `!launch <title> :: <task text>` (owner only).
- **Bound rooms:** in a room bound with `!bind`, a normal prefixed message (`!ai …`) becomes `aidevops sessions ask channel:matrix:<roomId>` instead of a runner dispatch. Unbound rooms keep today's runner path unchanged.
- **Outbox relay:** replies from sessions in `outbox/matrix/` are posted to their room and then acknowledged with `aidevops sessions outbox matrix --ack <id>`.

All bus calls go through the `aidevops sessions` CLI with `--origin chat:matrix:<roomId>` and `--actor <entity-id>` from the bot's existing entity resolution.

## Why

The Matrix bot can already create a fresh OpenCode session per prompt (`matrix-bot.mjs.template:168-194`), but it cannot reach a running session, see what sessions exist, or receive a session's reply later. The bus provides all three, and this bridge connects them, so the owner can work with live sessions from a phone.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The bus, trust and binding contracts are fixed by t18891 and t18892. This task is command parsing, CLI calls and a relay loop in an existing bot, following existing ingress patterns.

## Origin

- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** The owner named releases as a common need for session-to-session messaging. Evidence from this session on 2026-11-08: another session's release lane (source PR #37182) had created the tag `v3.39.136`, but its executor had died (`RELEASE_EXECUTOR` state `dead`, `process-absent`). This session only saw "A different source owns the active release lane", with no way to tell which session owned it or whether that session was still alive. It recovered with `aidevops release reconcile 37182` (provenance PR #37234). Its own merged PR #37165 went out in that release, but no session was told when the publication finished.

## What

1. **Lane owner session:** when a release lane is acquired, or its executor is captured or re-captured, record an advisory `owner_session: { session_id, captured_at }` from `AIDEVOPS_OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` (else `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`). It is informational only and never used for ownership, recovery or authority decisions.
2. **Held-lane hint:** when a release command is refused because another source holds the lane, print the owner session's handle, status and last activity from `aidevops sessions show <session_id> --json`. Then print a ready-to-run `aidevops sessions ask <handle> "…"` line. When the owner session is not live, say so next to the existing executor liveness line and recovery command.
3. **Release notices:** `aidevops sessions watch-release <owner/repo>` (and an `aidevops_sessions` `watch-release` action) subscribes the caller's root session. On `release_lane_finalize`, and when liveness first observes a dead executor for an active lane, a best-effort `info` notice goes to every subscriber and to the lane owner session. The notice carries the repo, source PR, tag, receipt or executor state, and the recovery command. Subscriptions expire after 7 days or once the session has no presence.

## Why

Release lanes already serialise publication safely, but sessions cannot see who holds a lane. The owner ends up relaying "is anyone releasing?" between sessions, and a dead executor is found only when someone else tries to release. Recording the owner session and sending notices turns those into one-hop questions over the bus.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** This touches release-lane state on a trust boundary. The new field must be provably advisory, and notices must never change release exit codes or timing.

## Relevant Files

title: t18897: Session bus ask with bounded wait, so subagents and scripts get the reply in ...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18897` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~4h`
**Logged:** 2026-11-08
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

Session bus ask with bounded wait, so subagents and scripts get the reply in the same call

## Done when

- [ ] `aidevops_sessions` `ask` with `wait_seconds` returns the matching reply in the same tool result when it arrives in time, and the reply is not delivered a second time to the root session.
- [ ] On timeout the call returns the ask ID and the reply later reaches the root session through normal delivery.
- [ ] Aborting the tool call ends the wait and releases the reservation.
- [ ] A subagent's message is framed for the recipient as from its root handle with `(via subagent <agent>)` appended.
- [ ] `aidevops sessions ask --wait N` prints the reply and acknowledges it in `outbox/cli` (exit 0), or exits 2 on timeout.
- [ ] Regression: asks without a wait, replies, and busy and idle delivery behave as before; the session-bus tests pass.
- [ ] Negative: a third concurrent wait in one root session is refused, and a reply whose `re` does not match the awaited ask is left for normal delivery.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- **Tool:** `sendAction` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs:69-84`) returns after `store.sendMessage`. For `ask` with `wait_seconds`, register the ask ID in a new `bus.awaitingReplies` map, then poll `store.pendingMessages(root, sender.sessionID)` every second for `type === "reply" && re === askId`. Claim it with `store.claimMessage` (rename, the existing at-most-once path), stop on timeout or `context.abort`, and always remove the reservation in `finally`. Add `wait_seconds: z.number().int().min(1).max(120).optional()` to the args (`:136-141`).
- **Reservation:** `claimPending` (`session-bus.mjs:199-202`) and the idle delivery in `session-bus-delivery.mjs` must skip entries whose `message.re` is in `bus.awaitingReplies`. The child and its root run in one OpenCode process, so an in-memory map is enough.
- **Attribution:** `bus.sender(context)` (`session-bus.mjs:242-247`) knows both `context.sessionID` and the resolved root. When they differ, add `via` to `from`. Render it in `senderLabel`/`frameMessage` (`session-bus-format.mjs:70-88`).
- **CLI:** `sendCommand` (`session-bus-cli-commands.mjs:81`) for `ask --wait N`. A shell sender has no inbox, so the reply goes to `outbox/cli` (`session-bus-messages.mjs:118-135`). Poll `store.readOutbox(root, "cli")` for `re === askId`, print it, then `ackOutbox` it. Exit 0 with the reply, or 2 on timeout, printing the ask ID.
- **Limits:** at most 2 concurrent waits per root session; extra waits are refused with a clear error. Waits send nothing extra and use no wake budget.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs`: `wait_seconds`, wait loop and abort handling.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs`: `awaitingReplies`, skip reserved replies in `claimPending`, and `via` in `sender`/`fromFor`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs`: skip reserved replies in idle delivery.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs`: `via` framing.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs` and `session-bus-cli.mjs`: `--wait`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs`: wait success, timeout, abort, reservation skip and `via` framing.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`: subagent behaviour and waits.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the `aidevops_sessions` tool (root and subagent sessions), `aidevops sessions ask`, the V1/V2 sidebars and compaction, which read `from` and must tolerate `via`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `sendMessage` (`session-bus-messages.mjs:104`) gains the optional `via`; the wait claims through `claimMessage`; the CLI wait acknowledges through `ackOutbox`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`.
- **Schemas/config:** message record `v: 1` with optional `from.via`; no new files or directories.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** not applicable because no new module is added; existing plugin files deploy through `setup.sh` as today.
- **Migrations/backfills:** not applicable because `via` is additive and old messages have none.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reservations live only in memory and are cleared in `finally`; rollback is a code revert.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `awaitingReplies` and the reservation skip in `claimPending` and idle delivery, with unit tests.
2. Add `wait_seconds` to the tool with the poll, claim, timeout and abort logic, and the concurrency limit.
3. Add `via` attribution and framing.
4. Add `--wait` to the CLI using the `cli` outbox.
5. Run the unit tests and the live self-test, and record the output in the PR.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** claim by rename stays the only delivery path, so the waiter and normal delivery can never both deliver the reply; the reservation only prevents the root from winning the race while a wait is active.
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored data changes beyond an optional field; rollback is a code revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** a recipient on an older plugin ignores `via` and replies normally; the reply still matches by `re`.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a retried wait on the same ask ID after a timeout can still collect a reply that has not been delivered yet.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the process exits during a wait, the reservation disappears with it and the reply is delivered to the root at its next turn as today.
- **Context cost:** the waiting tool call returns one framed reply (at most 2000 chars), the same size as normal delivery.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli-commands.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-cli.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs`
- `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-tool.mjs
```

- **Runtime evidence (self-test, no owner needed):** with `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR` set to a scratch directory and two `opencode serve` sessions A and B (t18886 "Live verification" setup), with B idle, check:
  - `aidevops sessions ask <B> "reply with the word pong" --wait 90` prints B's reply and exits 0, and `outbox cli` is empty afterwards.
  - In A, a subagent prompted to call `aidevops_sessions` `ask` to B with `wait_seconds: 90` gets B's reply in its own tool result.
  - B's framing shows "via subagent".
  - A `--wait 1` against a busy session exits 2 with the ask ID.
- **Surface mapping:** unit tests cover the reservation, wait, timeout, abort and framing. The live run covers the real wake, reply and the subagent tool path.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. The changes stay inside the plugin and its reference doc.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: t18897 ask wait for subagents`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** subagents stay out of presence and are never message targets; no change to wake limits, hop rules or sender identity; no change to agent tool permissions (which agent types may call `aidevops_sessions` stays as configured); chat-origin trust is t18891.

**AI brief owner:** the interactive owner session of t18886 (marcusquinn).

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-08
- **Session:** opencode:interactive ses_e480fcfa0ffeCzemlBnZ5j1VBA (t18886 session bus, GH#37149, PR #37165, released in v3.39.136)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** The owner asked whether subagents can message back and forth. In the released bus a subagent's `aidevops_sessions` call acts for its root session (`session-bus-identity.mjs:4-6,62-69`; `session-bus.mjs:242-247`). Only root sessions publish presence and receive delivery (`session-bus.mjs:189-190`; `session-bus-delivery.mjs:160-163`). A subagent can therefore send and ask as its root, but the reply lands in the root's inbox and never reaches the subagent that asked. Making subagents addressable would need presence for short-lived child sessions that cannot be woken mid-run, and the parent–child Task prompt and result already connect a parent and its child. The useful gap is a round trip inside one tool call.

## What

1. **`ask` with `wait_seconds`** (tool) and `--wait <seconds>` (CLI), from 1 to 120. After sending the ask, the call waits for a reply whose `re` is that ask's ID and returns the reply, framed as usual, in its own result. On timeout it returns the ask ID and says the reply will follow normal delivery. Cancelling the tool call (the abort signal) stops the wait.
2. **Reply reservation:** while a wait is active, the root session's busy and idle delivery skips that one reply, so the waiting call claims it. After the wait ends, the reservation is released and normal delivery resumes.
3. **Subagent attribution:** when the caller is a subagent, the message's `from` gains an advisory `via: { session_id, agent }`, and the recipient's framing reads `from <root-handle> (via subagent <agent>)`. The sender identity is still the root session.
4. **Docs:** `reference/session-bus.md` explains what subagents can and cannot do, and when to use `wait_seconds`.

## Why

A worker subagent that needs one fact from another live session (for example "is PR 123 releasing?" or "which branch holds this fix?") can ask today, but it never sees the answer. The root receives the reply later, after the subagent has finished. A bounded wait closes that loop at almost no cost: no new storage, no child presence, and the existing at-most-once claim.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** This is a contained change to the tool, CLI and delivery claim path, with one in-memory reservation set. Message formats change only by an advisory field.

title: planning-commit-helper.sh silently skips WIP-committed planning files
body:
## Observed

On 2026-11-08 an interactive session wrote seven task briefs and plan edits in a linked worktree and WIP-committed them, as `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Git workflow" asks ("After each logical change, commit WIP"). It then ran `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: …"` as `scripts/commands/new-task.md` Step 5 says. The helper only publishes planning paths that differ from `HEAD`:

- `has_planning_changes` uses `git diff --name-only HEAD` / `--cached` / untracked (`.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh:45-60`).
- `_planning_publish_changed_paths` uses the same three sources (`.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh:81-91`).
- With nothing uncommitted, the helper logs "No planning file changes to commit" (`planning-commit-helper.sh:583-584`) and succeeds.

So briefs committed as WIP are silently left out of the planning publication. Only uncommitted `TODO.md` ref edits would have been published. The session avoided this by running `git reset --soft <base>` before the helper (planning PR #37251 then carried all nine files).

## Expected

Planning files committed on the current branch but not yet on the default branch are included in the planning publication, or the helper refuses with a clear message naming them.

## Suggested fix

- In `planning-publisher.sh` `_planning_publish_changed_paths`, also include `git diff --name-only <merge-base with the remote default branch>..HEAD -- TODO.md todo/` when the current branch is not the default branch, so committed-but-unpublished planning paths join the snapshot. The snapshot already reads file content from the working tree, which matches `HEAD` for committed paths.
- Or, minimum: in `planning-commit-helper.sh`, before the "No planning file changes" exit, detect committed planning paths ahead of the remote default branch and print them with the exact recovery command, returning 1.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`

Change `_planning_publish_changed_paths` (around lines 81-91) and the no-changes exit (around lines 583-584). Extend the existing planning publisher tests; find them with `git ls-files '.agents/scripts/tests/*planning*'`.

## Verification

- In a scratch linked worktree, commit a new `todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md`, then run the helper with publication disabled or against a scratch remote (follow the existing planning publisher tests' setup). The brief must appear in the published snapshot, or the helper must exit 1 naming it.
- Existing planning publisher tests pass. ShellCheck is clean on both scripts.
