title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #37235 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #37235

**Parent issue:** #37235 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** Detect macOS user-lookup outage (id -un returns a number) and tell the user to restart instead of polling for hours
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,origin:interactive,tier:standard,consolidation-in-progress,fix-the-fixer`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #37235 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#37235 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 37235 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent.** Run all four commands below for #37235, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing). Do not close this consolidation task until every parent's handoff is complete:

```bash
gh issue comment 37235 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 37235 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 37235 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 37235 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #37235 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #37235.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What happened

On a macOS 26 host with 23.5 days of uptime (about 980 processes, load average about 16), macOS stopped resolving the logged-in user from about 06:15 UTC. This lasted until a forced restart about 6.5 hours later. Evidence from OpenCode session tool output:

- `id -un` printed `501` instead of the user name (06:20). `dscacheutil -q user -a uid 501` printed nothing (06:21).
- `ssh` and `git commit` failed with `No user exists for uid 501` (06:18–06:20).
- `pgrep` failed with `sysmon request failed with error: sysmond service not found` / `Cannot get process list`, while `sysmond` was still running.
- `dscl . -read` of the user's own record (attribute `UniqueID`) failed with `Operation failed with error: eServerError`. `launchctl print gui/501` failed with `Operation not permitted`.
- `gh` reported offline/unauthenticated and Playwright could not launch Chromium.

Interactive sessions kept polling (`sleep 240; id -un`) for hours, and background routines kept running. The lock screen later rejected the user's correct password, almost certainly for the same reason. The user had to reset the password in Recovery mode, which caused macOS to set the login keychain aside. Only a restart clears this state, and nothing in aidevops told the user that.

   - Non-macOS hosts always pass.
2. Pulse and routine pre-flight:
   - When the check fails, skip the cycle and log one WARN line.
   - Write one marker file and send at most one desktop notification per hour: "macOS cannot look up your user account; restart the Mac before entering your password at the lock screen". Use `osascript display notification`, and fail quietly if it can't run.
   - Do not dispatch workers while the check fails.
3. `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1443` sets `runner=$(id -un)`. Guard it so a numeric value is not used as a runner login.
4. Interactive sessions: add a short entry to `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` (or the nearest diagnostics reference). It should say: if `id -un` prints a number or tools report `No user exists for uid`, stop retrying, checkpoint, and tell the user to restart. Warn that the lock screen may reject the correct password while this lasts, and that the user should not reset the password in Recovery mode, because that sets the login keychain aside.

title: docs: ratchet-bump needs a new PR event before the required Qlty Regression Gate re-evaluates
body:
## What happened

On PR #37237 the `ratchet-bump` label was added after the required `Qlty Regression Gate` had already failed. The label started `qlty-regression-ratchet-refresh.yml`, which passed as `refresh / Qlty Regression Gate`. The required context `Qlty Regression Gate` stayed failed, because `qlty-regression.yml` no longer runs on `labeled` events (GH#31789) and a rerun keeps the original event payload, where `HAS_OVERRIDE` is false.

The required check passed only after a new `synchronize` event (a new commit). PR #35464 used a close and reopen for the same reason. Neither step is documented.

## Fix

Document the step in `.agents/tools/code-review/qlty.md` (Troubleshooting, after "Diagnosing a regression"): after a maintainer adds `ratchet-bump`, the required `Qlty Regression Gate` re-evaluates only on the next `opened`, `synchronize` or `reopened` event. Push the next commit, or close and reopen the PR. Rerunning the failed job is not enough. Also state that `refresh / Qlty Regression Gate` passing does not satisfy the required context.

Optionally, make the `qlty-diff` step's failure message in `.github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml` (the `::error::` line that suggests adding the label) mention the same step.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/code-review/qlty.md`
- `.github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml` (message text only, optional)

## Verification

- `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/tools/code-review/qlty.md`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml` if the workflow message changes.

title: consolidated: detect macOS user-lookup outage (numeric id -un), gate pulse dispatch, and advise restart
body:
_Supersedes #37235 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Detect the macOS "user lookup outage" state (`id -un` prints a numeric UID, `dscl . -read` of the current user's own record fails) and react safely:

1. A cheap shared check that fails only on macOS when user lookup is broken (non-macOS hosts always pass).
2. Pulse (and routine) pre-flight skips the cycle, logs one WARN line, writes one marker file, sends at most one desktop notification per hour, and dispatches no workers while the check fails.
3. `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` never uses a numeric `id -un` value as a runner login.
4. A short diagnostics entry tells interactive sessions to stop retrying, checkpoint, and tell the user to restart the Mac.

## Why

Observed incident (from #37235): on a macOS 26 host with 23.5 days of uptime (about 980 processes, load average about 16), macOS stopped resolving the logged-in user from about 06:15 UTC. This lasted until a forced restart about 6.5 hours later. Evidence from OpenCode session tool output:

- `id -un` printed `501` instead of the user name (06:20). `dscacheutil -q user -a uid 501` printed nothing (06:21).
- `ssh` and `git commit` failed with `No user exists for uid 501` (06:18–06:20).
- `pgrep` failed with `sysmon request failed with error: sysmond service not found` / `Cannot get process list`, while `sysmond` was still running.
- `dscl . -read` of the user's own record (attribute `UniqueID`) failed with `Operation failed with error: eServerError`. `launchctl print gui/501` failed with `Operation not permitted`.
- `gh` reported offline/unauthenticated and Playwright could not launch Chromium.

Interactive sessions kept polling (`sleep 240; id -un`) for hours, and background routines kept running. The lock screen later rejected the user's correct password, almost certainly for the same reason. The user had to reset the password in Recovery mode, which caused macOS to set the login keychain aside. Only a restart clears this state, and nothing in aidevops told the user that.

## How

Line numbers below were re-checked against `origin/main` at consolidation time; re-verify before editing (the parent cited `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1443`, which has since moved).

1. **Shared check** — add a small function (for example `_preflight_macos_user_lookup_ok`) in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh` next to the other `_preflight_*` helpers (e.g. `_preflight_capacity()` near line 304):
   - Return 0 immediately when `uname -s` is not `Darwin` (non-macOS hosts always pass).
   - Fail when `id -un` prints only digits (`[[ "$name" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]`), or when `dscl . -read` of the current user's own record (attribute `UniqueID`) fails.
   - Keep it cheap: no network, no `pgrep` (it also fails during the outage), bounded runtime. Shell rules: `local var="$1"`, explicit `return 0`/`return 1`, ShellCheck clean.
2. **Pulse and routine pre-flight gate** — call the check before any dispatch work in a cycle. `_run_preflight_stages()` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (near line 1471) is where cycle pre-flight begins (`_preflight_start_merge_first`, async cleanups, `calculate_max_workers`, then `_preflight_early_dispatch`); `main()` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (near line 1302) is the outer entry. Confirm which runs first per cycle and gate at the earliest point that precedes dispatch. When the check fails:
   - Skip the cycle and log one WARN line.
   - Write one marker file (reuse the existing advisory-file directory pattern used for `underfill-*.advisory` near `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1218`) and send at most one desktop notification per hour: "macOS cannot look up your user account; restart the Mac before entering your password at the lock screen". Use `osascript display notification`, and fail quietly if it can't run.
   - Do not dispatch workers while the check fails.
   - Routine pre-flight: the parent asks for the same gate on background routines. The routine runner path is not in the Files Scope; if wiring it requires a file outside the scope, follow `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery" rather than silently widening the scope.
3. **Runner login guard** — `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` currently sets `runner=$(id -un)` near line 1220 (parent cited line ~1443). Guard it so a numeric value is not used as a runner login (for example fall back to `$USER`/`$LOGNAME` when non-numeric, or skip the runner-attributed step).
4. **Interactive diagnostics entry** — add a short entry to `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` (or the nearest diagnostics reference): if `id -un` prints a number or tools report `No user exists for uid`, stop retrying, checkpoint, and tell the user to restart. Warn that the lock screen may reject the correct password while this lasts, and that the user should not reset the password in Recovery mode, because that sets the login keychain aside.
5. **Optional / not yet known** — where an OpenCode plugin hook could show the same advisory to interactive sessions. Search `.agents/plugins/` (e.g. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/`) before adding one; it is not in the Files Scope, so treat it as a follow-up unless scope recovery authorizes it.

Checkpoint recovery: none referenced. Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On non-macOS hosts the check always passes and pulse behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] With a stub `id` first on `PATH` that prints `501` for `-un`, one pulse cycle performs no dispatch, logs exactly one WARN line, and writes one marker file.
- [ ] A second run within the hour sends no additional notification (at most one `osascript display notification` per hour); a missing/failed `osascript` does not error the cycle.
- [ ] Without the stub, the pulse runs as before.
- [ ] `runner=$(id -un)` in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` never yields a numeric runner login.
- [ ] `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` contains the restart/no-Recovery-reset guidance described above.
- [ ] ShellCheck passes on the changed scripts and the existing pulse pre-flight tests pass.

## Verification

1. Put a stub `id` first on `PATH` that prints `501` for `-un`, then run one pulse cycle. Expected: no dispatch, one WARN line, one marker file, and no notification on a second run within the hour.
2. Without the stub, the pulse runs as before.
3. Run ShellCheck on the changed scripts and the existing pulse pre-flight tests (`rg -l preflight .agents/scripts/tests`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- ADD: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-macos-user-lookup.sh`

Integration scope recovery: `main()` evaluates routines before engine preflight, and `evaluate_routines()` can also be invoked independently. Gate the routine entry point before publication or dispatch. Add focused command-stub regression coverage for the macOS-only gate, bounded lookups and hourly notification suppression; verify with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-macos-user-lookup.sh`, existing pulse stage/routine tests and ShellCheck. No explicit hard boundary is widened.

## Context & Decisions

- Original problem statement, evidence, proposed fix, files and verification: #37235 (interactive session report).
- Per @alex-solovyev (fix-the-fixer detector, t3077): this touches the worker dispatch system itself, so workers run with `AIDEVOPS_VERBOSE_LIFECYCLE=1`, `WORKER_STALL_TIMEOUT=180`, and `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_PREFLIGHT_SENTINEL=1`. Remove the `fix-the-fixer` label if that classification is wrong.
- Per @alex-solovyev (large-file simplification gate, t2042): an earlier hold for `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`/`pulse-wrapper.sh` exceeding 2000 lines was cleared; both are now below 2000 lines on `origin/main` (1778 and 1977), so scoped edits are dispatchable.
- Consolidation correction: the `runner=$(id -un)` line has moved from ~1443 to ~1220 in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`.
- No requires-secrets runner prerequisites in the source issue.

title: t18899: buzz-aidevops: deploy the Buzz plugin to a stable non-versioned folder so updates reach Buzz
body:
## Task


Give the Buzz plugin `buzz-aidevops` a stable, non-versioned install folder so Buzz's local-folder watcher picks up each `aidevops update` automatically.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Give the Buzz plugin `buzz-aidevops` a stable, non-versioned install folder so Buzz's local-folder watcher picks up each `aidevops update` automatically.

## Why

`~/.aidevops/agents` is a symlink into a versioned bundle (`~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/<version>-<sha>-<ts>.<rand>/agents`). When a user adds the plugin from `~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops`, Buzz Preview resolves the symlink and saves the versioned path as the plugin's update source (profile `registry.json` → `installed["sh.aidevops.buzz"].currentSource.root`). Buzz polls that saved folder every 5 s for changes (block/buzz-app `src/app/PluginImport.tsx:320-331`). The next `aidevops update` repoints the symlink to a new bundle but leaves the old bundle unchanged, so Buzz never sees the new plugin.

Observed 2026-11-08: after PR #37237 (agent type) merged and `aidevops update` deployed 3.39.136, Buzz Preview 0.7.0-preview.254.1 still ran the phase-0 plugin. The saved source was the 3.39.135 bundle, the stored manifest had only the `buzz-status` command, and the `aidevops` agent type was missing from the harness picker. Users get no error; the new features just never show up.

## How

1. In setup's agent deploy, copy `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/` to a real (not symlinked) directory outside `runtime-bundles/`, for example `~/.aidevops/plugins/buzz-aidevops/`. Replace files in place with an atomic per-file rename so Buzz never reads a half-written folder. Pattern: the existing deploy steps in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` (bundle handling near `bundles_dir`, ~1032).
2. Point the README install table at the stable path, and add a one-time migration note: in Manage plugins → aidevops → Update plugin, choose the new folder. Buzz only allows replacing an installed plugin's source through that plugin's own update control (`PluginImport.tsx:366` treats a fresh Add as "Already installed").
3. Optional: make `aidevops buzz status` warn when Buzz's saved source for `sh.aidevops.buzz` sits under `runtime-bundles/`. Read the profile `registry.json` under the user's Buzz application-support folder (`xyz.block.buzz.desktop` / `.dev`). Print only the path classification, never other registry content.

The README install table is at lines ~30-36.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/README.md`
- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- After `setup.sh --non-interactive`, `~/.aidevops/plugins/buzz-aidevops/{manifest.json,plugin.js}` exist as regular files matching `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/`, and `readlink` on that directory prints nothing.
- Run a second deploy with a changed `plugin.js`: the stable folder updates in place and its path is unchanged.
- README names the stable path and the one-time Update-plugin step.
- ShellCheck clean on changed scripts; `.agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh` passes.

## Verification

`setup.sh --non-interactive`, then `ls -la ~/.aidevops/plugins/buzz-aidevops` and `diff -r .agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops ~/.aidevops/plugins/buzz-aidevops`. Manual: in Buzz Preview, use Update plugin to point at the stable folder, run `aidevops update` after a plugin change, and confirm the plugin revision changes within a few seconds with no manual step.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: t18898: Session bus for Buzz-hosted agents: labelled presence, remote provenance and ...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18898` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~6h`
**Logged:** 2026-11-08
**Tags:** `feat` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

Session bus for Buzz-hosted agents: labelled presence, remote provenance and safe delivery

**Blocked by:** `t18891`

## Done when

- [ ] Step 1 evidence is recorded in `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md`: a remote-interactive ACP process publishes presence (or the task stops with the evidence).
- [ ] A remote-hosted session's presence has `interface` and `agent`, and `aidevops sessions list` shows the label. Local session records are unchanged.
- [ ] Messages from a remote-hosted session carry a `chat:` origin and never wake a local session; replies to its asks arrive in its own inbox.
- [ ] A message to a remote-hosted session never triggers a wake and is delivered on its next chat-started turn.
- [ ] Negative: a malformed or missing overlay context yields `chat:remote:agent` and no wakes, never `opencode`.
- [ ] Regression: local TUI and serve sessions keep their current wake, origin and presence behaviour; all session-bus tests pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- **Detection:** `index.mjs:361` already loads the team-interface conversation. Pass `isRemoteInteractiveConversation(conversation)` (`team-interface-context.mjs:93`) and the overlay's agent ID and `interface_context` into `createSessionBusHooks` (`session-bus-plugin.mjs:17`), then into `createSessionBus`. Do the same in `v2.mjs:373` (`createV2SessionBusHooks` in `session-bus-v2.mjs:106`). The overlay's `context` property (`.agents/schemas/team-interface/opencode-launch-overlay-v1.schema.json:156`) holds the `interface_context` refs (definition at `:24-60`); confirm how the loader exposes it. Do not read `BUZZ_*` variables: the remote boundary strips them (`team-interface-remote-boundary.mjs:107`).
- **App and channel:** app = the `provider_ref` value after `provider:`, lower-cased and checked against the chat app part of `CHAT_ORIGIN` (`session-bus-files.mjs:38`). Channel = the `conversation_ref` value after `conversation:`, if it matches the channel part. Otherwise use the agent ID. If neither is valid, use app `remote` and channel `agent`. Never fall back to `opencode`.
- **Presence:** add `interface` and `agent` to the record in `PresencePublisher.record` (`session-bus-presence.mjs:99-117`), only when set, so local records stay byte-identical. Show them in `session-bus-format.mjs` rows and `show` output.
- **Sender:** `fromFor` (`session-bus.mjs:230-239`) returns the chat origin when the bus is remote-hosted.
- **Delivery:** `canWake` (`session-bus-delivery.mjs:55-58`) returns false when this process is remote-hosted. Pending messages still deliver through the user-turn path (`index.mjs:739-742`, `sessionBus.chatMessage`) and the tool-result path. Senders already see "delivered at the recipient's next turn" semantics for `info`. For an `ask`, add one line to the send result when the recipient record has `interface` set, for example `this session is driven from buzz; it answers on its next chat turn`.
- **Docs:** add a "Remote-hosted sessions" section to `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`, and one line to the Buzz plugin README "How a turn runs" list.

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`: pass the remote-interactive context to the bus hooks.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2.mjs`: the same for OpenCode 2.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-plugin.mjs`: accept and forward the option.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-v2.mjs`: forward the option.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus.mjs`: remote flag, chat origin in `fromFor`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-presence.mjs`: `interface` and `agent` fields.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-delivery.mjs`: no wake into a remote-hosted session.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-bus-format.mjs`: "via" label in rows, `show` and the ask notice.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-session-bus.mjs`: unit cases for the three behaviours.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/session-bus.md`: remote-hosted sessions section.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/README.md`: one line on bus messages.
- EDIT: `todo/plans/opencode-session-bus.md`: Phase 3 table row for t18898.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `aidevops sessions list|show` (`session-bus-cli-commands.mjs`), the `aidevops_sessions` tool, the TUI sidebar (`tui-messages.mjs`), and t18895 coordination readers. All read presence and treat the new fields as optional.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** presence writes in `PresencePublisher` (`session-bus-presence.mjs`); message `from` built by `fromFor` (`session-bus.mjs:230`) and written by `sendMessage`/`sendReply` (`session-bus-messages.mjs:104,121`); wake claims in `deliverToIdle` (`session-bus-delivery.mjs:95`).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`; `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-team-interface-remote-interactive-profile.mjs`; the ACP canary pattern in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-installed-startup.mjs`.
- **Schemas/config:** presence record gains two optional fields at the same `v`; no message schema change (origin is already a free string validated by `CHAT_ORIGIN`).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none; no new modules, so the `agent-deploy.sh` freshness list is unchanged.
- **Migrations/backfills:** not applicable because presence records are rewritten on every publish and messages expire after 7 days; nothing persisted needs conversion.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the plugin change; `PresencePublisher` (`session-bus-presence.mjs`) rewrites each record on its next publish, so stale `interface` and `agent` fields disappear without a cleanup step.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Confirm the premise (self-test):** with `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_BUS_DIR` set to a scratch directory, start a remote-interactive ACP process the way the installed-startup canary does (`opencode-launcher-helper.sh remote-interactive --overlay … --dir … --session-id …`, or the canary's own spawn). Send ACP `initialize` and `session/new`, then confirm a presence record with `kind: "acp"` appears. Record the result in the plan. If no presence appears, stop. Update this brief and the issue with the evidence, because the premise is false.
2. Plumb the remote context through the hooks (V1 and V2).
3. Add presence fields and the chat-origin sender.
4. Add the `canWake` guard and the ask notice.
5. Unit tests, docs, then rerun step 1 and verify the three behaviours live.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** no new shared files. Presence and message writes keep `writeJsonAtomic`.
- **Migration/rollback:** additive optional fields; rollback is a revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** an older CLI ignores unknown presence fields. An older local plugin treats `chat:` origins as non-waking, the same as the new code, so mixed versions are safe in both directions.
- **Idempotency/retry:** no new retries. Messages that skip a wake stay pending until the next chat-started turn or the 7-day retention prune.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the overlay context cannot be parsed, the process still counts as remote-hosted (origin `chat:remote:agent`, no wakes). It never falls back to local defaults.
- **Trust boundary:** mark the remote-hosted guard in `canWake` and `fromFor` with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Never derive the remote flag or origin from model-supplied tool arguments.
- **Overlap:** t18891 (GH#37244, in progress) changes chat-origin wake rules (verified-actor opt-in wakes) in the same files. Rebase on it and keep its opt-in from applying to remote-hosted senders, unless its verified-actor check passes.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-08
- **Session:** opencode:interactive ses_e480fcfa0ffeCzemlBnZ5j1VBA (t18886 session bus, GH#37149, PR #37165, released in v3.39.136)

- **Conversation context:** The owner wants aidevops usable from chat apps (SimpleX, Matrix, Buzz) and asked for every self-testable follow-up to be filed. Matrix and SimpleX adapters are t18893 and t18894. While scoping a Buzz adapter, code reading showed that Buzz-hosted agents are probably already session-bus endpoints. Their current defaults (wakes and `opencode` sender origin) were designed for local terminal sessions. This task makes them safe and visible first. Posting bus replies into Buzz channels stays with the Buzz plugin work in t18883 (GH#36976, owner-gated).

## What

Treat an OpenCode process started by the remote-interactive launcher (`AIDEVOPS_REMOTE_INTERFACE=1`, `remote_interactive_v1` overlay) as a remote-hosted bus endpoint:

1. **Labelled presence:** its presence record gains additive fields `interface` (for example `buzz`, from the overlay's `provider_ref`) and `agent` (the overlay agent ID). `aidevops sessions list`, `show` and the sidebar show "via Buzz agent …", so local sessions can tell a chat-driven agent from a terminal session.
2. **Remote provenance:** messages it sends carry origin `chat:<app>:<conversation>` (built from `provider_ref` and `conversation_ref`) instead of `opencode`. The existing rule that chat origins never wake a session (`session-bus-delivery.mjs:21-23`) then applies, so a chat-driven turn cannot wake the owner's local sessions. Its replies still arrive in its own inbox, because `sendReply` routes by sender session ID first (`session-bus-messages.mjs:123-128`).
3. **No wakes into it:** messages to a remote-hosted session wait for its next turn started from the chat app. They never trigger a bus wake, because a turn the chat app did not start has no channel to answer in (see Hazards).

## Why

Code-path evidence suggests remote-interactive Buzz agents already publish presence and get `aidevops_sessions`, with the same defaults as a terminal session:

- The restricted conversation profile returns early, without the bus (`index.mjs:366-368`). The remote-interactive profile continues to `createSessionBusHooks` (`index.mjs:445-451`).
- `opencode acp` is a messageable kind (`session-bus-files.mjs:34`, `session-bus-presence.mjs:23-30`).
- The launcher keeps HOME (`opencode-launcher-helper.sh:1770-1797`), so `busRoot` (`session-bus-files.mjs:42-45`) is the shared bus.

Two defaults are then wrong:

- **Wakes into the agent:** a woken turn runs inside the ACP process, but the Buzz plugin only posts the reply for the turn it started. `recordUpdate` keeps text for any known session (`.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js:324-332`), and the plugin posts plain text as the reply (`.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/README.md:68-69`). The woken turn's output is therefore lost, or leaks into the next channel reply.
- **Wakes from the agent:** Buzz starts turns for the owner's messages and for messages the owner attested (`README.md:57-58`). With origin `opencode`, those turns can wake local owner sessions, which the chat trust model reserves for verified owner actors (`.agents/reference/team-interface-trust.md`, t18891).

None of this is verified live yet; step 1 confirms it before any change.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The design is decided here and reuses existing chat-origin and reply rules. The work is a plugin-option plumb-through, two delivery guards, display fields and one ACP self-test.

## What

Add a macOS account and login-keychain incident reference for aidevops agents: how to triage a rejected login password or an unexpected screen-sharing indicator, how to recover after a Recovery-mode password reset sets the login keychain aside, and how to recover app data such as WireGuard tunnels that live in the old keychain.

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`
**Detected topic:** Cleanup and preservation contract
**Current size:** 500 lines

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Worker guidance

**Reference pattern:** `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md` (playbook for splits — covers orchestrator pattern, identity-key preservation, and PR body template).

**Precedent in this repo:** `issue-sync-helper.sh` + `issue-sync-lib.sh` (simple split) and `headless-runtime-lib.sh` + sub-libraries (complex split). For agent docs, see existing chapter-file splits in `.agents/reference/`.

**Expected CI gate overrides:** If this PR triggers a complexity regression from restructured files, apply the `complexity-bump-ok` label AND include a `## Complexity Bump Justification` section in the PR body citing scanner evidence. See the playbook section 4 (Known CI False-Positive Classes).

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md' | grep -c . | grep '^0$' >/dev/null` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)

Automated scan flagged this file for review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

title: perf(pulse): pulse REST overhead exhausts 5000/h core quota on shared runners; workers starve
body:
## What

On the shared Linux runner, the pulse's own REST overhead uses up most or all of each account's 5,000/hour core quota before workers get any. When a runner hits 0 remaining, it dispatches nothing until the quota resets. In the last 24 hours this cut the managed `<webapp>` repo's throughput from 242 merged PRs a day to 70.

## Evidence (shared host, v3.39.136, 2026-11-08 23:55Z)

- Runner B (`alexey`): core `remaining=0 used=5000`, `pulse-health.json` shows `workers=0/32 dispatched=0`, `dispatch=deferred`. 87 issues are available.
- Runner A (`vladimir`): core `remaining=2103 used=2897` with 9 workers. `pulse.log` has 67 `budget exhausted` and 17 `primary_cooldown` in the last 4,000 lines.
- Last 60 minutes of REST rows in `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` (column 3 = `rest`), runner A / runner B:
  - `pulse-wrapper.sh rest-core-selected`: 1,396 / 1,837
  - `pulse-merge-routine.sh rest-core-selected`: 901 / 724
  - `pulse-wrapper.sh rest-response-owned`: 561 / 239
  - `pulse-merge-routine.sh pulse-review-explicit-page`: 441 / 165
  - `pulse-wrapper.sh explicit-rest-pagination`: 411 / 132
  - `collaborator-permission-rest` across `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`, `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` and `pulse-wrapper.sh`: 835 / 154. `_gh_current_user_allows_repo_write` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh:458` deliberately does not cache (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`), and it also calls `gh api user` each time.
- Pulse cadence: runner B's systemd timer is 120s, runner A's is 180s. `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh api-budget` reports `risk=watch reason=fast_timer_detected_without_lock_skip_evidence`, and `shared_dir=no` for the PR-view cache on both.
- `gh-api-calls.log` rows carry no endpoint or family column, so `rest-core-selected` can't be attributed further without new instrumentation.

## How

1. **Attribution first.** Add a privacy-safe endpoint *family* column (for example `repos/:o/:r/pulls`, `.../collaborators/:u/permission`, `user`) to `gh-api-instrument.sh` rows, and report the top families in `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh api-budget` for a 60-minute window. Files: `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-api-budget.sh`.
2. **Collaborator permission.** Keep the trust boundary, but memoise `gh api user` and the permission result within one process, keyed by the active token's credential fingerprint (see `credential_identity` in `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py`). If the token rotates, the key misses, so a stale login can never authorize a different token. File: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`, add `#aidevops:trust-boundary` on the new check.
3. **Reserve for workers.** Make the pulse's optional stages (merge-routine review pages, explicit pagination) defer once remaining core falls below a reserve, for example 20% of the limit, so dispatch and running workers keep quota. Reference: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-budget-policy.sh`.
4. Once item 1's attribution names the top families, fix them (cache, conditional requests or cadence).

## Acceptance

- `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh api-budget` lists the top REST endpoint families for the last 60 minutes.
- With `collaborator-permission-rest`, a pulse cycle makes at most one lookup per (token, repo), verified by a test with token rotation that shows a cache miss.
- On a runner at the reserve threshold, optional pulse stages log a deferral while dispatch continues. Runner core quota no longer reaches 0 in steady state, checked with `gh api rate_limit` over 3 consecutive hours.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/gh-api-instrument.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-api-budget.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-budget-policy.sh`

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.core|[.remaining,.used]|@tsv'` as the runner account, then `awk -F'\t' -v cut="$(($(date +%s)-3600))" '$1>=cut && $3=="rest"{k[$2"  "$6]++} END{for(x in k) print k[x]"\t"x}' ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log | sort -rn | head`

**Actual output:** `0	5000` on runner B, with the pulse callers totalling about 3,000–5,000 REST rows in the last hour (top rows shown under Evidence). Pulse health reports `workers=0/32 dispatched=0`.

**Expected:** the pulse stays well below the hourly quota and leaves a reserve, so dispatch continues.

**Parent issue:** #37273 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`

**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,priority:critical,tier:thinking,origin:interactive,consolidation-in-progress,fix-the-fixer`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #37273 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#37273 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 37273 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash

  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent.** Run all four commands below for #37273, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing). Do not close this consolidation task until every parent's handoff is complete:

```bash
gh issue comment 37273 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 37273 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 37273 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 37273 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #37273 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #37273.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

title: docs: read bounded-operation output before recording claims derived from it
body:
## Problem

An interactive session ran a read-only browser verification through `aidevops_bounded_operation`, read only the first part of its terminal output (the setup lines), and then wrote the expected verification result into durable records: a brief ledger, a work log, a commit and a PR body. The output slice that would have confirmed the result was never read. Later the operation generation had expired (`operation is unavailable or belongs to an expired generation`), so the original evidence could not be recovered. A later rerun confirmed the result only at a later data state, and the earlier rendered value stays unconfirmed.

The bounded-operation reference already says generations expire on restart, reload or disposal (`.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md`, "Bounded interactive operations"). It does not state the consequence for evidence: once a generation expires, any claim written from an unread output is unverifiable.

## Proposed change

Add one short paragraph after the `output` retrieval paragraph in `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md` ("Bounded interactive operations"), roughly:

> Read the output slice that proves a claim before writing that claim into any durable record (ledger, work log, commit message, PR or issue body). A passing exit code or the first lines of output are not evidence of a specific assertion. Retrieval depends on the in-memory generation, which can expire on reload or restart; if a claim's evidence was not read before expiry, record it as unconfirmed and rerun the read-only check rather than restating it.

Optionally add a matching one-line rule to `.agents/reference/session.md` near the guidance that treats summaries as point-in-time evidence (around "Treat summaries and checkpoints as point-in-time evidence").

## Files

- `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md` (primary)
- `.agents/reference/session.md` (optional cross-reference)

## Verification

- `rg -n "before writing that claim" .agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md` finds the new paragraph.
- The always-loaded `AGENTS.md` size ratchet is unaffected (reference-only change).
- Markdown lint used for `.agents/reference/` passes.

title: t18902: buzz-aidevops: plugin version and an update-ready nudge in the Settings card
body:
## Task


Give the buzz-aidevops plugin a visible version, and have its Settings card tell the user when `aidevops update` has deployed a newer plugin that Buzz has not loaded yet.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Give the buzz-aidevops plugin a visible version, and have its Settings card tell the user when `aidevops update` has deployed a newer plugin that Buzz has not loaded yet.

## Why

Owner test 2026-11-09 on Buzz Preview 0.7.0-preview.254.1: a plugin fix was copied into the watched folder `~/.aidevops/plugins/buzz-aidevops`, but Buzz kept running the old revision and the owner had no way to tell. Reading block/buzz-app source (`5d9d1ef33c`):

- Buzz versions installed plugins by a content-hash `revision`. The manifest has no version field (`src/plugins/api.ts:6-18`).
- A local-folder plugin is checked for changes only while its detail panel in Settings → Manage plugins is open and visible (`src/app/PluginImport.tsx:293-331`, 5 s poll). Nothing checks in the background.
- An update always needs the user to press **Update** and review access (`PluginImport.tsx:720-747`; `src/app/Settings.tsx:990-994`). That is deliberate and should stay.

So updates do reach the folder, but users don't know to open the panel. A version number plus a nudge in our own card closes that gap.

## How

1. In `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js`, add `const PLUGIN_VERSION = "x.y.z"` (start at `1.1.0`: phase 1 plus the field fixes). Bump it by hand only when plugin files change, so unchanged `aidevops update` runs don't change the revision and don't prompt users. Show it in the Settings card ("aidevops plugin 1.1.0").
2. In `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh` (`aidevops buzz status`), print one line `Buzz plugin deployed: <version>`, read from the deployed `~/.aidevops/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js` with a fixed-pattern match on the `PLUGIN_VERSION` line. Print `not deployed` if missing.
3. In the card, compare `PLUGIN_VERSION` with that line. If the deployed version is newer, show: "A newer aidevops plugin (X) is ready. Open Settings → Manage plugins → aidevops and press Update."
4. README: add a short "Updating" section covering the version, the nudge, and that Buzz only checks while the plugin's panel is open.
5. Optional: a check in `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` or the existing plugin test that fails when `plugin.js`, `manifest.json` or `README.md` change without a `PLUGIN_VERSION` change. Skip it if there is no cheap existing hook.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/plugin.js`
- `.agents/plugins/buzz-aidevops/README.md`
- `.agents/scripts/buzz-desktop-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- The card shows the plugin version.
- With an older plugin loaded in Buzz and a newer one deployed, the card shows the nudge; with matching versions it does not.
- `aidevops buzz status` prints the deployed version line and nothing from Buzz's private profile files.
- ShellCheck clean; `.agents/tests/test-buzz-desktop-helper.sh` passes; Biome and `node --check` clean on `plugin.js`.

## Verification

Bump `PLUGIN_VERSION` in a worktree, deploy with `setup.sh --non-interactive`, open Settings → aidevops in Buzz Preview, and confirm the nudge. Then press Update in Manage plugins and confirm the nudge clears.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

This issue body is composed under `.agents/workflows/brief.md`. Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

title: stats-health-dashboard: timed-out repos rejoin the back of the rotation and go stale past the 48h freshness threshold
body:
## Observed

A supervisor health dashboard on a managed repo went stale for 2d23h, which tripped `dashboard-freshness-check`. The launchd `stats-wrapper` job ran hourly with exit 0 the whole time. The refresh code path is healthy: a manual run of `_update_health_issue_for_repo` for the affected repo finished with `rc=0 stage=complete` in 45s and published `last_refresh`.

## Root cause (evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log` and the per-repo schedule cache)

1. **The fixed 60s per-repo bound (`STATS_HEALTH_REPO_TIMEOUT`) has no headroom under REST pressure.** At nominal speed a refresh already takes about 45s (session-time 13s, `_gather_health_stats` 5s, body edit 3s, title edit 10s, maintenance 10s). In the last scheduled attempt, `.attempt=1794170870` and `.stage=body-publication|1794170916`: data-gather took 46s, and the body write was then killed at 60s. `[gh-cooldown] primary-core active=true` was logged in the same run.
2. **A timed-out repo goes to the back of the whole rotation.** `_order_health_repo_entries` sorts by `max(attempt, last_refresh)`, so a failed attempt counts the same as a success for scheduling. Each hourly run spends its health budget on the priority repo (`marcusquinn/aidevops`, which also hits `rc=124` almost every run), the aggregate caches, and then only 1–3 rotation repos. With about 67 pulse repos, a repo's next turn comes about 25 runs later, roughly 1–2 days.
3. Result: since 2026-10-21, every turn this repo got ended in `rc=124` (`data-gather`, `issue-resolution`, `body-publication`, or `maintenance`). One failed turn plus one full rotation is longer than the 48h freshness threshold. The same alert class has recurred (GH#30106–GH#30129, GH#31582). Earlier fixes (GH#31576, GH#31585) added stage checkpoints and publish-before-maintenance ordering, but did not change the capacity math.

## Expected

A dashboard whose last successful refresh is getting close to the freshness threshold should get a bounded recovery attempt before it goes stale. A permanently failing repo must not be able to monopolise the run.

## Worker guidance

Files:

- `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`: `_order_health_repo_entries` (around line 533), `_refresh_health_repo_bounded` (around line 556), `_update_health_issues_with_session_cache` (around line 714).
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh` (existing timeout and ordering coverage, from GH#31576).

Suggested approach (keep it bounded and minimal):

1. **Recovery lane:** when `${cache}.refresh-state` is older than a recovery age (for example `STATS_HEALTH_RECOVERY_AGE_SECONDS`, default 24h, half the freshness threshold) **and** the last attempt did not succeed (`attempt > refresh epoch`), place at most one such repo straight after the priority repo. Pick the one with the oldest successful refresh. Leave normal rotation unchanged for everything else.
2. **Recovery timeout:** give that repo an extended bound (for example `STATS_HEALTH_RECOVERY_REPO_TIMEOUT`, default 120s). It must still be capped by `_HEALTH_WORK_DEADLINE` through `_stats_run_bounded`, so the aggregate budget never grows.
3. Optional: log per-repo elapsed seconds in the `stopped for` line, so future triage does not need to read cache files.

Do not raise `STATS_TIMEOUT` and do not add new GitHub calls.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-wrapper-timeout.sh` passes. Extend it only if needed to prove that one recovery repo is ordered after the priority repo and that a second recovery candidate keeps normal ordering.
- After deploy, the next `stats.log` cycle shows the recovery repo refreshed, or a `stopped for` line with elapsed time.

Ref: alert issue on a managed repo (dashboard-freshness-check generator); private repo names withheld.

title: Pulse auto-merge: scoped trust for github-actions[bot] starter-sync issues (core-files diff only)
body:
## What

Let pulse worker-briefed auto-merge accept PRs that resolve a **starter-sync** issue (filed by a plugin repo's own `.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml` as `github-actions[bot]`) without a per-issue `sudo aidevops approve issue N`, using a **scoped** trust check like the OpenCode pin-canary one (GH#35752), not a blanket `github-actions[bot]` entry in `trusted-issue-authors.conf`.

## Why

Plugins made from WP Plugin Starter (for example `wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent`) run a daily `starter-sync.yml` that opens one issue titled `Core files differ from the starter` with label `starter-sync`. Its author is `github-actions[bot]` (`author_association=NONE`), so the t2449 gate in `_attempt_worker_briefed_auto_merge` blocks the resolving PR until a maintainer signs (observed: wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent#147 / PR #173, merged only after `sudo aidevops approve issue 147`).

The maintainer asked for these to pass automatically. A plain `github-actions[bot]` line in `.agents/configs/trusted-issue-authors.conf` would do it, but `_is_trusted_issue_author` matches the login only, globally: every Actions-filed issue in every pulse-managed repo (including workflows that act on untrusted triggers, such as issue triage gates with `issues: write`) would skip the author gate, and the file ships to every aidevops install. The pin-canary exception shows the intended pattern: bind bot trust to the exact issue shape and the PR's file scope.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh`: add `_is_trusted_starter_sync_issue_pr pr_number repo_slug issue_api`, modelled on `_is_trusted_opencode_canary_issue_pr` (lines ~119-172). Mark it `#aidevops:trust-boundary`. Fail closed on any API error, truncated file list (>= 100 files) or missing data. Require:
   - issue `.user.login == "$_PM_WORKFLOW_BOT_LOGIN"` and `.user.type == "Bot"`, title exactly `Core files differ from the starter`, labels include `starter-sync`;
   - every changed PR file is listed in the target repo's `scripts/core-files.txt` read at the PR **base** ref (`gh api repos/{slug}/contents/scripts/core-files.txt?ref=<baseRefOid>`), or is `changelog.txt`; no renames or deletions outside that list;
   - optional hardening the worker should evaluate: for core files without plugin-own marker blocks (`<!-- *-own:start -->` / `# *-own:start`), the PR head blob equals the starter's blob at the commit the issue names. If that proves impractical, record why in the PR.
2. Call it in `_attempt_worker_briefed_auto_merge` next to the canary branch (lines ~437-457), with a matching `[pulse-merge]` log line. Keep all other gates (checks, reviews, review-bot, NMR, hold-for-review, draft) unchanged.
3. Leave `.agents/configs/trusted-issue-authors.conf` unchanged; add one comment line there pointing bot-filed issue trust to scoped checks.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/configs/trusted-issue-authors.conf` (comment only)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh` (cases below)

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process-worker-briefed.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-briefed-trust-parity.sh` pass, with cases: starter-sync issue + in-scope diff passes; wrong title, missing label, non-Bot author, or a file outside `scripts/core-files.txt` fails; API failure fails closed.

## Acceptance

- A PR resolving a `github-actions[bot]` starter-sync issue whose diff stays within the repo's `scripts/core-files.txt` (+ `changelog.txt`) passes the t2449 author gate without a signature.
- Any other `github-actions[bot]` issue still needs OWNER/MEMBER authority, the allowlist, the canary scope, or a signature.

title: issue-sync: generated issue body keeps provisional task ID after renumber; sync-body cannot resolve mapping
body:
## Observed

In a private managed repo, two issues created together on 2026-11-03 have generated bodies whose `**Task ID:**` and `Blocked by` values differ from the issue title and the TODO.md row:

| Title / TODO.md | Body `Task ID` | Body `Blocked by` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tA` (e.g. t1747) | `tA+7666` (t9413) | n/a |
| `tB` (e.g. t1748) | `tB+7666` (t9414) | `t1744,t9413` (should be `t1744,t1747`) |

A sibling issue created the same day (`t1744`) has a correct body. TODO.md rows carry the correct IDs with `ref:GH#NNN`. The constant offset suggests the bodies were composed from a provisional or colliding task-counter allocation that was later renumbered in TODO.md, without regenerating the issue body.

## Impact

1. The issue body misstates the task ID and its blockers.
2. `issue-sync-helper.sh sync-body tB --repo <owner/repo> --dry-run` (run from a canonical checkout synced to main, where TODO.md has `ref:GH#NNN` for `tB`) fails with `sync-body requires an immutable task/ref mapping for tB`. The stale body therefore cannot be repaired through the supported body-only path.
3. The push-to-main issue-sync workflow (push/close/enrich steps) does not refresh existing non-plan issue bodies after a brief changes, so a widened brief never reaches the issue.

## Expected

- Issue bodies use the final allocated task ID. If an ID is renumbered after issue creation, the body is regenerated.
- `sync-body` resolves the issue from the TODO.md `ref:GH#NNN` when the coordinator mapping is missing or disagrees, or it reports the specific mismatch (coordinator mapping vs TODO ref vs body task ID).

## Pointers

- `issue-sync-helper-body.sh` `cmd_sync_body` → `resolve_task_gh_number` (`issue-sync-lib-ref.sh`, coordinator `resolve-issue`, then TODO `ref:GH#` fallback).
- Task ID allocation: `claim-task-id.sh` via `planning-commit-helper.sh next_task_id`.

## Verification

1. Run `sync-body` for an affected task and confirm it either succeeds or names the exact mapping conflict.
2. Confirm a renumbered task's issue body shows the TODO.md task ID after sync.

Workaround used: edit the title manually, and add a comment pointing to the brief as the authoritative source.

title: fix(hostinger): origin-block check and per-client model for LiteSpeed 403 refusals
body:
## What

Add a read-only `hostinger-helper.sh origin-block` check and correct `services/hosting/hostinger.md`: the "LiteSpeed reCAPTCHA refusing all visitors" entry describes a **per-client-address** refusal, not a site-wide outage.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-09, one shared account, ~40 WordPress installs behind Cloudflare)

- For about 22 minutes every site on the account answered the 787-byte LiteSpeed `403` ("Access to this resource on the server is denied!", `x-turbo-charged-by: LiteSpeed`) to the operator workstation, **static files included**. It then dropped back to the `/.lsrecap/recaptcha` "Bot Verification" challenge on dynamic pages only, and then cleared.
- **Direct request from the host to its own origin (`--resolve`): `200`.** Through Cloudflare from the workstation: `403`.
- **Cloudflare GraphQL `httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups` by `clientIP`, uncached:**
  - The workstation address had 202 × `403` in one 5-minute bucket.
  - Outside visitors' addresses were mostly `200` in the same window.
  - The other `403`s were single scanner addresses.
- So the refusal is keyed on the real client address (LiteSpeed reads the Cloudflare client IP) and applies across every vhost on the server. The operator's browser shares the workstation address with every parallel AI session, so "every site is down" was true only from that address.
- **Trigger, consistent with 7 earlier observations (5–6 Nov):** the account was near its CPU limit (bulk imports, multisite cron runners, fleet deploys). The workstation sent bursts of scripted HTTP: up to ~1,000 requests in 5 minutes across sites on the same server, much of it headless Chrome or curl verification.
- **The problem feeds itself:** a client without JavaScript cannot pass the challenge, so every retry is another failed try and extends the hard deny. A curl status loop used for diagnosis keeps the block in place.
- The 6 Nov doc entry ("refused every outside visitor") was measured from the workstation; it now reads as a public outage, so sessions treat it as one.

## Reproducer

While the block is active, run from the operator workstation:

1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://<host>/robots.txt` returns `403`, and the body contains "Access to this resource on the server is denied".
2. The same request for any other site on the account also returns `403`.
3. On the host, `curl -sk -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --resolve <host>:443:<host egress IPv4> https://<host>/robots.txt` returns `200`.
4. Cloudflare GraphQL `httpRequestsAdaptiveGroups`, filtered to `cacheStatus` not hit and grouped by `clientIP` and `originResponseStatus`: the `403`s concentrate on the workstation address, while other addresses get `200`.

## How

1. `hostinger-helper.sh origin-block HOST [--ssh ALIAS] [--wait SECONDS] [--interval SECONDS]`. Read-only, bounded, prints no IP addresses:
   - **Public probe:** one static request (`/robots.txt`). Only if that is not blocked, one cache-busting dynamic request. Each body is classified as `denied` (block-page marker), `challenge` (`/.lsrecap/`), `timeout` (LiteSpeed `408`) or `ok`.
   - **With `--ssh`:** a direct request from the host to its own origin, bypassing Cloudflare. The script is sent on stdin, and the egress IPv4 is read from Cloudflare's `/cdn-cgi/trace` on the host, so no address is printed.
   - **Verdict and exit code:** `ok` 0, `refused-client` 10 (this address is refused; the site is up), `refused-origin` 11 (the origin refuses the host too), `site-error` 12, `inconclusive` 13.
   - **`--wait`:** re-checks at most once per `--interval` (default 60 s, minimum 30), static request first, until `ok` or the time limit.
2. `hostinger.md`: replace the "refusing all visitors" entry with a per-client model covering:
   - the deny → challenge → clear sequence;
   - diagnosis: run `origin-block` first, then Cloudflare analytics per `clientIP`;
   - prevention: pace scripted HTTP per account, stop on the block page, prefer WP-CLI or host-side direct-origin checks, never loop curl;
   - the shared-address impact on the operator's browser.

   Keep the 408 and "server's own requests" entries, and link them.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`: new `origin_block_command` and helpers, dispatch case, help line. Follow the `image_libs_command` pattern (remote script over `ssh -o BatchMode=yes … 'bash -s'`, alias validation).
- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`: the "LiteSpeed cache" bullets around the reCAPTCHA / 408 entries.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh` clean.
- `hostinger-helper.sh origin-block <host> --ssh <alias>` on a live account prints a verdict and exits 0 when clear.
- Unknown option or bad host → usage and exit 1.
- Markdown lint passes on `hostinger.md`.

title: t18905: Session bus for workers: messageable headless workers, worker presence and pulse steering relay
body:
## Task


1. **Headless workers are messageable (same user, same machine).** `send` and `ask` to a worker (`kind: headless`) are accepted from the tool and CLI. Workers receive messages at their next tool result or turn, exactly like busy interactive sessions. Workers are never woken, get no poll timer and no `aidevops_sessions` tool (no schema cost); they answer asks through the CLI.
2. **`aidevops sessions reply <msg-id> <text>`.** A CLI reply for shells inside an OpenCode session (the worker's Bash tool), using the session ID from the shell environment. Asks delivered to a headless session say how to reply with the CLI.
3. **Worker presence.** Headless records gain `worker` (issue, repo, attempt, tier from the dispatch environment). Every root record gains `tool` (`name`, `since_epoch`) while a tool runs. `list`/`show` label workers and show a long-running tool.
4. **Worker finished notices.** `notify-when-idle` accepts a worker. When its run ends the subscriber gets one notice naming the worker, its last task and the issue to check.
5. **Pulse steering relay.** A new `worker-bus-relay-helper.sh relay`, run as an optional pulse stage, checks each live worker's issue at most every 2 minutes (one REST call when nothing changed) and sends that worker one pointer message when:
- a maintainer adds a comment (collaborator author, not bot, not a worker/pulse machine comment; interactive-session comments count),
- the issue is closed,
- the issue gains `hold-for-review`.
The message names the comment ID and the exact `gh` command to read it; it never copies GitHub text into the bus.

## Done when

- [ ] `aidevops sessions send <worker>` succeeds and the worker sees the framed message at its next tool result; no wake is attempted.
- [ ] Headless processes get no `aidevops_sessions` tool and no poll timer.
- [ ] `aidevops sessions reply <ask-id> <text>` inside a session shell answers an ask; outside one it fails with a clear message.
- [ ] Headless presence carries `worker` from the dispatch env; records carry `tool` while a tool runs.
- [ ] `notify-when-idle` on a worker delivers one notice when the worker's run ends.
- [ ] Relay sends one pointer per new maintainer comment batch, close and hold; skips worker/pulse machine comments, bots and non-collaborators; respects the per-worker interval; `AIDEVOPS_WORKER_BUS_RELAY=0` disables it.
- [ ] Regression: existing session-bus tests pass; ShellCheck clean.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- **Messageable workers:** `MESSAGEABLE_KINDS` gains `headless` (`session-bus-files.mjs:34`). `SessionBus` adds `wakeable = messageable && kind !== "headless"`; the poll timer, `deliverToIdle` and wakes require `wakeable` (`session-bus.mjs:72`, `session-bus-delivery.mjs:59-64`). `addTool` skips headless (`session-bus-plugin.mjs:40-42`).
- **CLI reply:** `replyCommand` next to `sendCommand` (`session-bus-cli-commands.mjs:110`), reusing `store.findReceived` and `store.sendReply` (`session-bus-messages.mjs:128`). `frameMessage(message, { cliReply })` gives the CLI form of the ask guidance (`session-bus-format.mjs:71-76`); the bus passes it for headless recipients.
- **Presence:** `workerContext(env)` from `WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER`, `WORKER_REPO_SLUG`, `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_ID`, `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_TIER` (set by `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:1762-1784`); added in `PresencePublisher.record` (`session-bus-presence.mjs:99-124`). `toolBefore` hook in V1 (`index.mjs:772`) and V2 (`v2.mjs:480`) records the running tool; `toolAfter` clears it.
- **Labelled shell sender:** `--sender <label>` for sessionless CLI senders (rejected inside a session); the sent/ key becomes `cli-<label>` so the relay has its own rate budget.
- **Relay:** new `.agents/scripts/worker-bus-relay-helper.sh` with `relay` and `status`; state in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/worker-bus-relay/`. Pulse stage via `_pulse_run_optional_stage_with_timeout` (REST/GraphQL budget-deferred) after `reap_orphan_workers` (`pulse-wrapper.sh:1033-1036`).
