title: t18927: fix(runner-health): keep a zero-attempt streak across window expiry so slow-failing runners trip the breaker
body:
## Task


The per-runner zero-attempt breaker (`.agents/scripts/pulse-runner-health-helper.sh`, t2897)
counts consecutive zero-attempt outcomes and trips at
`RUNNER_HEALTH_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` (default 10). Any real attempt resets the
counter, so it is already a streak. However, `cmd_record_outcome` (lines 369-375)
also zeroes the counter when `_rh_window_expired` (lines 323-335) reports that
`RUNNER_HEALTH_WINDOW_HOURS` (default 6) have passed since `window_started_at`,
even when no real attempt happened in between. A runner that fails more slowly
than 10 dispatches per 6 hours never trips, keeps claiming issues, and fails
every one.

Make the window measure idleness of the streak, not its age: expire only when
the last zero-attempt outcome is older than the window. Equivalently, re-anchor
`window_started_at` on every zero-attempt outcome. A real attempt still resets
the streak. Also confirm the release reason seen below is recorded as a
zero-attempt signal; if it is not, map it.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-runner-health-helper.sh`. In `cmd_record_outcome`,
  apply window expiry only when the most recent zero-attempt outcome in
  `.last_outcomes` (or a new `last_zero_attempt_at` field) is older than
  `RUNNER_HEALTH_WINDOW_HOURS`. On a zero-attempt outcome, set that timestamp.
  Keep `window_started_at` semantics for `status` and `diagnose` output, or
  update both to show the streak anchor. Keep state schema v1 readable: a
  missing new field means "use `window_started_at`".
- Trace which `record-outcome` signal the `worker_failed` release path sends
  (callers: `headless-runtime-failure.sh` via `_HRFF_RUNNER_HEALTH_HELPER_OVERRIDE`
  and `pulse-cleanup.sh:461` `_record_runner_health_zero_attempt`). If a worker
  that exits within about 90 s with no branch, no commit and low tokens is
  recorded as a non-zero signal, map it to `low_token_usage` or
  `no_branch_created`. Do not count provider rate limits as zero-attempt; they
  have their own backoff.
- Do not change the threshold default, the update-and-resume recovery, routine
  signing handling (lines 361-367), or the per-runner scope.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops

## What

The per-runner zero-attempt breaker (`.agents/scripts/pulse-runner-health-helper.sh`, t2897)
counts consecutive zero-attempt outcomes and trips at
`RUNNER_HEALTH_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` (default 10). Any real attempt resets the
counter, so it is already a streak. However, `cmd_record_outcome` (lines 369-375)
also zeroes the counter when `_rh_window_expired` (lines 323-335) reports that
`RUNNER_HEALTH_WINDOW_HOURS` (default 6) have passed since `window_started_at`,
even when no real attempt happened in between. A runner that fails more slowly
than 10 dispatches per 6 hours never trips, keeps claiming issues, and fails
every one.

Make the window measure idleness of the streak, not its age: expire only when
the last zero-attempt outcome is older than the window. Equivalently, re-anchor
`window_started_at` on every zero-attempt outcome. A real attempt still resets
the streak. Also confirm the release reason seen below is recorded as a
zero-attempt signal; if it is not, map it.

## Why

Public audit comments on `marcusquinn/aidevops` issues updated 2026-11-09
12:00Z-18:50Z (`Dispatching worker` paired with `CLAIM_RELEASED` by `claim_id`):

- One runner device had 9 dispatches and 9 `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_failed`
  releases, median 89 s from dispatch to release, across 4 issues
  (#32446, #37247, #37375, #37382). Its dispatches continued from 13:39Z to 17:17Z
  through four aidevops versions (v3.39.144 to v3.39.147). #37375 alone took 4 of
  these failed attempts.
- Over the same period other runner devices completed 8 issues
  (#37307, #37373, #37374, #37386, #37391, #37394 and others) with
  `worker_complete`, including one using the same model as the failing device
  (`openai/gpt-6.1-terra`), so the fault is device-local, not model-wide.

  reset in `cmd_record_outcome` restarts the count before it can trip.

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-runner-health-helper.sh`

  the breaker.
- Ten zero-attempt outcomes where the gap between two of them exceeds the
  window do not trip (an idle runner still decays).
- A real-attempt outcome anywhere in the sequence resets the streak, as today.
- An existing state file without the new field keeps working.

## Verification

  cases using `RUNNER_HEALTH_TEST_NOW`.

  `test-pulse-wrapper-runner-health.sh` stay green.

title: gh-write-helper.sh comment --edit-last can overwrite an older comment on long issues
body:
## Observed

`gh-write-helper.sh issue comment <N> --repo <owner/repo> --edit-last --body-file <file>` passes `--edit-last` straight to `gh issue comment`. On a long issue (several hundred comments), gh edited an **older** comment by the same user (created two days earlier), not the comment posted seconds before. The older comment's content was overwritten.

Recovery used GraphQL `IssueComment.userContentEdits` (the earliest edit's `diff` holds the original body) and a targeted `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/{id}`.

## Likely cause

`gh issue comment --edit-last` selects the "last" comment from a limited or paginated comment fetch. On long threads that may not be the newest comment.

## Proposed fix

- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`: reject `--edit-last` for `comment`, or resolve the exact newest own comment ID and require an explicit `comment edit <comment-id>` subcommand that PATCHes by ID.
- `reference/gh-command-discipline.md`: edit comments by ID, never with `--edit-last`.

## Verification

On an issue with more than 100 comments, posting a comment and then editing it through the helper changes only that comment ID; `--edit-last` is refused with guidance.

title: aidevops secret NAME -- cmd drops trailing '=' from injected values
body:
## Problem

`aidevops secret NAME -- <command>` injects the value with trailing `=` characters removed. Base64 secrets with padding (common for 32-byte keys such as KMS master keys) then reach the command corrupted, without any error.

`aidevops secret set` stores the value intact; only the injection/read path is lossy.

## Reproduction (aidevops 3.39.147 agents / 3.39.148 CLI, macOS, gopass backend)

```bash
printf 'canary-value-xyz=' | aidevops secret set AIDEVOPS_CANARY_TRAILING_EQ
aidevops secret AIDEVOPS_CANARY_TRAILING_EQ -- sh -c 'printf "%s\n" "${#AIDEVOPS_CANARY_TRAILING_EQ}"'
# prints 16 (expected 17)
gopass show -o aidevops/AIDEVOPS_CANARY_TRAILING_EQ | wc -c
# 17: the stored value is intact
```

Observed while escrowing a 44-character base64 key (one `=` of padding): the SHA-256 of the injected value differed from the source; the SHA-256 of `gopass show -o` matched.

## Expected

The injected environment value is byte-identical to the stored value, including trailing `=`.

## Likely location

The `secret` run/exec path in the aidevops CLI and secret helper: look for parsing of `KEY=VALUE` lines (for example splitting on `=`, `cut -d=`, `${line%%=*}`/`${line#*=}` with greedy patterns, or trimming of `=`). The exact file is not verified: reads of the secret helper are blocked by the secret-read guard in agent sessions.

## Verification

Run the reproduction above; the length must be 17. Also round-trip `abc==` (length 5) and a value containing an inner `=` (`a=b`).

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`
**Detected topic:** Cleanup and preservation contract
**Current size:** 500 lines

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Worker guidance

**Reference pattern:** `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md` (playbook for splits — covers orchestrator pattern, identity-key preservation, and PR body template).

**Precedent in this repo:** `issue-sync-helper.sh` + `issue-sync-lib.sh` (simple split) and `headless-runtime-lib.sh` + sub-libraries (complex split). For agent docs, see existing chapter-file splits in `.agents/reference/`.

**Expected CI gate overrides:** If this PR triggers a complexity regression from restructured files, apply the `complexity-bump-ok` label AND include a `## Complexity Bump Justification` section in the PR body citing scanner evidence. See the playbook section 4 (Known CI False-Positive Classes).

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md' | grep -c . | grep '^0$' >/dev/null` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

### Dispatch authority

This issue was created under verified maintainer authority and is ready for automated dispatch. No additional approval comment is required.

Teach the Hostinger agent how to work on a client's own Hostinger account through hPanel **Account sharing**, where the agency has Collaborator (or Admin) access but no password.

Agencies building and maintaining client sites need SSH and WP-CLI on the client's plan. The public Hostinger API has no Account-sharing endpoints, and a shared plan with no website has no SSH. title: t18929: fix(lifecycle): let a session relinquish its own run so long-lived OpenCode p...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18929` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug`

## Outcome

fix(lifecycle): let a session relinquish its own run so long-lived OpenCode processes stop pinning finished worktrees

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Let an interactive session explicitly relinquish its own lifecycle run on a worktree it has finished with. Then long-lived OpenCode app processes stop pinning merged worktrees and release checkouts until the app quits. Wire the relinquish into the owning session's explicit worktree removal.

## Why

Per-repository dispatch fails closed when live worktrees reach the cap (`pulse-dispatch-core.sh:195-214`, default 200). On one Pulse host (2026-11-09 ~19:55Z, counts only) the aidevops repo had 259 live worktrees. Every aidevops dispatch candidate was rejected at `dedup.worktree_cap`: 7 of 7 pre-launch rejections in a 30-minute window, 0 spawns, 18 free slots.

Classifying the 259 by what holds their lifecycle generation (read-only registry query):

- 68 are bound to a **live** `opencode` process: 5 distinct app processes, 16-24 h old, one holding 44. 41 of these are release tag, preparation or control checkouts that inherited the interactive runtime identity before GH#37365. The rest are interactive feature or bugfix worktrees whose PRs are typically merged.
- 15 are bound to dead PIDs with stale `alive` observations (handled by GH#37424).
- 84 have all runs ended; 77 have no generation file or no runs (legacy and observation-era classes).

Without the 68 live-process pins the repo is at 191 (<200) and dispatch reopens.

Root cause: `shell-env.mjs:251-252` declares `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID = process.pid` (the OpenCode app process) and the session ID. `admit_session` (`worker_lifecycle/session.py`) derives `run_id` from generation, session and identity, so runs are already session-scoped. But a run only ends when the native process exits, and all sessions in one OpenCode app share that PID. Finishing, closing or rolling over a session releases nothing; only quitting the app does.

## How

1. Registry: `relinquish-session --path PATH --pid PID --session-id ID`. Recompute the run_id exactly as `admit_session` does. Require the PID to be an ancestor of the invoking process (`caller_ancestors` in `cleanup_plan.py`). Record an `ended` observation with reason `session-relinquished`. Never touch other runs of the generation. Idempotent. #aidevops:trust-boundary.
2. Callers: explicit `worktree-helper.sh remove` opts in. When retirement reports `waiting-for-caller`, relinquish the caller session's run on that path, then retry retirement once.
3. Re-admission: relinquish is permanent; a later `admit-session` by the same session refuses with `session-owner-already-ended`, and the plugin explains it.
4. Docs: CLEANUP.md documents the verb.

## Implementation note (PR #37449)

- Delivered: items 1-4. Runtime-verified in a live OpenCode session. Before the change, the deployed remove refused with `waiting-for-caller`; with it, the same tree relinquished and retired archive-first.
- Deferred: release-tree inherited bindings. The release reaper runs outside the owning runtime's process ancestry, so the ancestor gate correctly refuses there; those trees still retire when the app exits.
- Deferred to t18930 (GH#37448): the `full-loop-helper.sh complete` handoff, which also holds a legacy owner PID checked by Pulse.

## Acceptance

- A session that merged a PR can remove its own clean worktree in the same session (no "retirement completes after this session exits").
- Another session in the same OpenCode process that is still bound to the same tree keeps it retained.
- A process that is not the bound runtime (not an ancestor) cannot relinquish.
- Existing lifecycle tests pass; focused cases are added to existing test files (no new runner).

## Verification

- `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests -v` (CI entrypoint in `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`) and `shellcheck` on touched shell files.
- Manual: in an interactive session, create a worktree, run a command in it, then run `worktree-helper.sh remove <path>`. Expect `status: retired`, not `waiting-for-caller`.
- Pulse host: `Live worktree count N >= cap` lines stop for aidevops once pins clear.

Ref #37022 (caller self-binding; caller not auto-excluded), #37365 (release executor ownership), #37424 (reaper starvation).

### Files Scope

- .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/session.py
- .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py
- .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_plan.py

- .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_enrollment.py
- .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_admission.py
- .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_retirement.py

</details>

title: chromium-debug-use-helper: detect a launched browser left stale by an on-disk update (new tabs crash)
body:
## Problem

A browser started with `chromium-debug-use-helper.sh launch` keeps running after Brave or Chrome updates itself on disk. From then on, every new tab in that browser crashes or stays blank: the old browser process cannot start renderers from the replaced framework. Existing tabs keep working, so the failure looks random. In our case it looked like a conflict with another session's browser profile, which it was not.

Observed on macOS: profile `infra-setup` started at 10:57 on Chromium 156.0.8078.80. Brave updated the app bundle at 11:50 to 1.99.55 (Chromium 157.0.8103.39). After that, `open` returned a target that never loaded, `navigate` timed out on `Page.enable` / `Runtime.enable` or returned `net::ERR_ABORTED`, and manual new tabs crashed for any site. `launch-stop` followed by `launch` on the same profile fixed it, and logins persisted.

## Expected

`launch` (reuse path), `launch-status`, `open` and `navigate` compare the running browser's version (`/json/version` `Browser`) with the installed app version. When they differ, they print a clear warning such as "browser updated on disk since launch (156 → 157); new tabs will fail; run launch-stop then launch". Optionally, `launch` could restart automatically when no tabs are open.

## Likely location

`.agents/scripts/chromium-debug-use-helper.sh`: the `launch` reuse branch and `launch-status`. On macOS the installed version is in `<App>.app/Contents/Info.plist` `CFBundleShortVersionString`. Brave's `Browser` string carries the Chromium version, so compare against the framework's `Versions/Current` target or the app bundle's modification time against the process start time.

## Verification

Start a profile, update or replace the browser app (or change the bundle's modification time in a test), then run `launch-status` and `open`: the warning appears. After `launch-stop` and `launch`, it does not.

title: t18930: fix(full-loop): release a finished interactive session's worktree ownership at the complete handoff so Pulse can retire merged trees while the app runs
body:
## Task


When an interactive session finishes a full loop (`full-loop-helper.sh complete`, the `CLEANUP_DEFERRED` handoff), let it release both locks it holds on that worktree. Then the guarded Pulse cleanup can retire the tree while the OpenCode app keeps running. Today the tree is kept until the whole app quits.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

When an interactive session finishes a full loop (`full-loop-helper.sh complete`, the `CLEANUP_DEFERRED` handoff), let it release both locks it holds on that worktree. Then the guarded Pulse cleanup can retire the tree while the OpenCode app keeps running. Today the tree is kept until the whole app quits.

## Why

An OpenCode app serves every session under one PID, which is `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID = process.pid` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/shell-env.mjs:251-252`). Two independent owner checks pin finished trees to that long-lived PID:

1. Lifecycle registry: the session's admitted run stays `bound` until the PID exits, so `prepare-cleanup` reports `waiting-for-runs` (`.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup_plan.py:139-145`).
2. Legacy owner / cleanup receipt: `complete` records `owner_pid` from `_resolve_worktree_owner_pid` or `$PPID` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh:695-702`). The merge path does the same in `_merge_record_deferred_cleanup_owner` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh:542-552`). Pulse removal skips while `_worktree_owner_alive` holds (`.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal-central.sh:149-155`).

GH#37432 adds `worker-registry.py relinquish-session` and wires it only into explicit `worktree-helper.sh remove`, which consults the registry alone. It does not change the `complete` handoff. Point-in-time evidence on one host (counts only), from the aidevops repo: 259 registered worktrees against a dispatch cap of 200. About 70 trees were bound to 5 live `opencode` processes, and the dispatch log reported `Live worktree count N >= cap` more than 700 times. Dispatch spawned 0 workers in a 30-minute window with free slots.

## How

- Prerequisite: t18929 (GH#37432) merged on `main`. If `relinquish-session` is absent from `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py`, stop and report blocked rather than reimplementing it.
- In `cmd_complete` (`full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh` ~690-735), after the receipt is durable, end this session's own registry run for the current worktree. Reuse the GH#37432 shell gate `_worker_lifecycle_relinquish_caller` in `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh`, or add a small `worker_lifecycle_relinquish_session <path>` wrapper there. It needs `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID` and `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_SESSION_ID` and must never fail the handoff.
- Make the receipt or legacy owner check accept the session's explicit end: for example, record the owner session plus a `relinquished` marker in the receipt. Then `_worktree_owner_alive`, or the receipt lease check, treats that owner as finished even though the runtime PID lives. Keep fail-closed behaviour for every other case.
- Design constraint: once the handoff relinquishes, the session must not need the tree again. Re-admission refuses with `session-owner-already-ended`, and the plugin now explains that. Document this in `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` step 9.
- Out of scope; record a decision in the PR: trees pinned by earlier sessions of a still-running app that never ran `complete`. Ending those needs OpenCode session-liveness evidence (`aidevops_sessions list`), not PID liveness.

## Acceptance

- After `complete` in an interactive session, a Pulse cleanup pass retires the merged tree, with archive-first retirement unchanged, while the OpenCode app is still running.
- A tree whose session did not run `complete` is still retained while its runtime lives.
- Headless workers are unchanged: their runtime exits at completion.

## Verification

- `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s .agents/worker-lifecycle/tests -v` with `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle`.
- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-cleanup-branch-merged-owned-skip.sh` (existing; no new runner).
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.
- After release: count `Live worktree count N >= cap` lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` and the registered worktree count against the cap.

Ref #37432 (relinquish primitive), #37022 (caller self-binding), #37424 (release reaper starvation).

- .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh
- .agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh

title: fix(pulse): exclude successful PR handoffs from worker failure totals
body:
## Objective

Stop reporting successful worker-to-PR handoffs as worker failures or stalls in Pulse current-state diagnostics. Keep a PR handoff distinct from merged delivery.

## Observed evidence

During live worker recovery on 2026-11-09, the current-state helper produced this internally inconsistent summary for a 15-minute window:

```json
{"worker_result_counts":{"post_pr_handoff":1},"worker_failures_or_stalls":1}
```

Separately verified healthy lifecycle evidence: issue #37433 completed with `exit_code=0`, `result=post_pr_handoff`, and ready PR #37447. All five required PR checks subsequently passed. This was not a failed or stalled worker, and the PR was not yet merged when inspected.

The source confirms the reporting cause:
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state.py:272-284`: `classify_metric()` preserves `post_pr_handoff` as its own class.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state.py:972-974`: `worker_failures_or_stalls` sums every class other than `success`, including healthy handoffs.
- The human-readable summary consumes that total, so consumers must not have to infer failures by subtracting known healthy classes themselves.

This is separate from #37431, which concerns rejecting legitimate PR-less review-triage completion in the headless runtime.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh`
- Read-only reference: `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh` and the existing headless-runtime outcome contracts for successful handoffs versus nonterminal continuation events.

## Implementation guidance

Use explicit outcome semantics for the failure/stall aggregate rather than treating every non-`success` class as a failure. Preserve raw `worker_result_counts` and genuine failure, rate-limit, and stall visibility. A successful PR handoff must not imply a merged PR or closed issue. Preserve existing JSON consumers where feasible; if a separate handoff total is useful, keep its meaning explicit. Do not suppress actual failures or modify worker execution, ownership, dispatch, or merge protections.

## Acceptance and verification

1. A worker metric with `result=post_pr_handoff` and `exit_code=0` remains visible but does not increment `worker_failures_or_stalls`.
2. Existing failed, rate-limited, and watchdog-killed fixture assertions continue to pass.
3. The text summary and JSON agree about failures/stalls versus handoffs.
4. Add the focused case to the existing helper test fixtures; do not introduce a runner, test-only API, or broad test infrastructure.
5. Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh`, relevant existing Python/shell lint, and `git diff --check`.

Prework discovery for these target files and `pulse-current-state post_pr_handoff worker_failures_or_stalls` found no matching recent commits, PRs, or claimed issues. The issue-creation wrapper should still perform its normal title deduplication. Keep all public evidence free of host-specific paths and sensitive logs.

title: fix: read provider credential configuration without shell execution
body:
## Problem

`resolve_api_key` in `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh` sources the entire plaintext credential configuration while checking provider availability. An unrelated assignment with an output redirection can therefore create files in the caller's working directory. Other shell statements can execute and mutate the probe's environment. A provider lookup should read a selected value, not execute configuration.

This is evidenced by current tracked source and an isolated synthetic regression. No real credential configuration is required to reproduce the source-level defect.

## Implementation scope

- Replace that fallback with `credentialFileSecret` from the existing `.agents/scripts/secret-resolver.mjs` parser, without changing the shared parser or the shared shell resolver.
- Preserve environment, gopass, plaintext configuration, then OAuth lookup order and source classifications.
- Extend the existing `tests/test-model-availability.sh` suite with synthetic HOME/files and direct resolver assertions: unrelated commands, redirections, substitutions and output must not execute; unrelated variables must remain unchanged; aliases, quoting, duplicate assignments, tenant selection, missing values and parser failures must retain safe behavior.
- Keep the existing OAuth fallback when the parser or Node runtime is unavailable. Plaintext parsing requires Node; executable shell-derived values are intentionally no longer evaluated by this path.

## Verification

title: fix: keep session checkpoints from entering the Pulse lifecycle
body:
## Problem

Read-only session finalization invokes the Pulse lifecycle launcher instead of a read-only observer. This crosses a consequential execution boundary and can also execute legacy credential-file shell syntax during a checkpoint.

## Verified evidence

- On aidevops v3.39.147, `session-distill-helper.sh auto` calls `session-checkpoint-helper.sh continuation` through `emit_checkpoint`.
- `.agents/scripts/session-checkpoint-helper.sh` sets `supervisor_helper` to `pulse-wrapper.sh` and executes `bash "$supervisor_helper" list --active` in `_gather_continuation_state` (installed lines 713–715). The state collection path has another positional `list --active` invocation.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` sources the legacy credential shell file at top level before command dispatch (installed lines 434–449). At its entry point, only `--command` selects the command facade; other positional arguments fall through to `main "$@"` (installed lines 1982–1988). `list --active` is not a supported facade command in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-commands.sh`.
- Static source inspection therefore establishes that a checkpoint can enter lifecycle initialization instead of a read-only list operation. No additional Pulse execution is needed to verify this defect.
- During the observed finalization, three zero-byte, same-owner, untracked artifacts appeared in the caller's working directory. Their timestamps matched the collector invocation. A non-executing, in-memory structural analysis matched all three names to shell redirection targets in local legacy credential assignments. Actual names, values, account identifiers, project identifiers and raw transcript content are deliberately omitted. The artifacts were removed only after ownership, zero size, regular-file type and invocation-time metadata were verified. The credential configuration was not changed.
- The bounded parent also drained surviving descendants after the collector exited. This is containment evidence, not proof of a persistent worker or of any external mutation. No unobserved dispatch or hosted-data action is claimed.
- The current remote checkpoint source still contains the unsupported call: blob `994700d4311a18160f5fc8a343e0d3a754493758`.

## Scope and implementation targets

1. Make checkpoint/state gathering use an existing genuinely read-only observer, or add a narrowly scoped read-only facade if none exists. It must not invoke the lifecycle launcher, source credential shell code, dispatch work, run routines or start background children.
2. Validate unsupported positional CLI arguments in `pulse-wrapper.sh` before credential loading or lifecycle side effects. Preserve explicitly authorized existing Pulse command behavior.
3. Inspect both checkpoint call sites, not just `continuation`.
4. Preserve compact checkpoint receipts and resumable failure reporting. Do not silently turn missing observer data into lifecycle execution.

Primary files: `.agents/scripts/session-checkpoint-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-commands.sh`. Reference the command facade's existing usage/error return pattern and the checkpoint collector's existing optional-state behavior. Discover the suitable existing shell regression files under `.agents/scripts/tests/`; their exact names have not been verified here.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/session-checkpoint-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-checkpoint-repo-scope.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh`

## Verification

- Use only a disposable synthetic HOME and a harmless sentinel credential assignment for a focused existing-harness regression. Never reproduce against an operator's real credentials or live Pulse configuration.
- Prove that continuation/state collection and unsupported positional arguments neither source the synthetic credential file nor create its sentinel redirection target, invoke lifecycle/dispatch/routine functions, make network calls or leave descendants.
- Prove that valid explicitly selected existing Pulse commands still route correctly under controlled stubs.
- Run ShellCheck on changed scripts and the relevant existing checkpoint, distillation and command-facade regression suites. No new runner, daemon, telemetry, broad browser matrix or CI gate is needed.

## Privacy and authority boundaries

The fix must not read or publish real credential values, alter operator credentials, rotate accounts, change hosting, or require a release. Local credential remediation and any account rotation remain separate operator-authorized actions. This report contains only sanitized structural evidence.

## Related discovery

Searches across open and closed issues for the checkpoint/Pulse call combination found no exact current report. #15543 concerns older supervisor-reference migration; it is context, not evidence that this current read-only-boundary defect is fixed.

title: t18932: fix(screen-time): stale macOS source renders 0h instead of unavailable for unobserved periods
body:
## Task


On macOS, a profile README period with no screen-time observations is published as `0h` when the live source is `stale`. It should show `unavailable`. This is the same class as the Linux before-first-sample fix (GH#36709 / GH#36737): an unobserved period is unknown, not zero.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

On macOS, a profile README period with no screen-time observations is published as `0h` when the live source is `stale`. It should show `unavailable`. This is the same class as the Linux before-first-sample fix (GH#36709 / GH#36737): an unobserved period is unknown, not zero.

## Why (evidence)

- The maintainer profile README render at 2026-11-08T02:13Z showed `Screen time (macOS) | 0h | 69.4h | 294.7h | ~3768h*`, with the note `Screen time from macos-knowledge-db:/display/isBacklit; collection status: ok, stale`. The previous render showed 17.6h for the prior day and 93.4h for the week. The wrong 0h stayed published for about 18.6h, until the next render at 2026-11-08T20:50Z. At the time the user was active (5.7–6.7h interactive attention per day).
- Repro on `main` (`dccc247faf`): a collection with `status: stale`, `latest_epoch` 36h before the start of yesterday, intervals only earlier in the week, and an empty history passed to `profile_payload()`. Result: `day: 0.0 stale source-observations coverage_days 0.0`.
- Cause: in `.agents/scripts/screen_time_history.py`, `bounded_period_payload()` computes hours whenever status is not `unavailable`. `coverage()` returns `(0.0, 0.0)` when nothing was observed in the window and `latest_epoch < start`. `apply_short_history()` cannot backfill, because the snapshot deliberately omits unobserved stale dates (test: `snapshot omits unobserved stale dates and records explicit zero-event dates`). The result is a measured-looking 0h.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_history.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh`

## How

1. In `bounded_period_payload()`, when the status is not `unavailable`, `observed_since` is `None`, and `coverage()` returns 0 observed days, set `status, reason = "unavailable", "no-observations-in-period"` and `hours = None`. A fresh source always has `latest_epoch >= start`, so coverage is at least 1 day. Explicit zero-event days from a fresh source therefore still show `0h`.
2. Keep Linux sampler behaviour unchanged. It uses `observed_since_epoch`, and `before-first-sample` already covers its unobserved periods.
3. Add one assertion beside the existing stale or sparse cases: a stale source with no in-window observations gives an `unavailable` day, and a fresh zero-event day still gives `0h`.

## Acceptance

- A stale macOS source with no observations in a period renders `unavailable (no-observations-in-period)`, not `0h`.
- The existing case `empty sources, explicit zero, and relative sparse-source selection are distinct` still passes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh profile-stats | jq '.periods.day'
```

</details>

title: fix(pulse): floor-path product reservation holds the only slot with processed=0 while product candidates are all skipped
body:
## What

In the dispatch floor path (`effective_slots=1`), the product reservation keeps the only slot held for hours while no candidate is assessed. Every cycle logs `processed=0/59`, so neither product nor tooling work launches. Make the reservation release once the product phase has made no verified launch and has no unknown outcome. Keep product prioritisation, every maintainer and terminal-blocker hold, and incomplete-discovery safety.

## Observed evidence

One runner on 2026-11-09, `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, framework version 3.39.150:

- At about 18:58Z GitHub REST core was exhausted for the runner login (`gh-cooldown primary-core ... github-core-primary-exhausted`). From then on, every cycle logs `Dispatch floor path engaged (throttle file present): limiting implementation batch to 1 (runtime degraded)` and `entering candidate loop with effective_slots=1, max_parallel=1, candidates=59`.
- The same three lines then repeat for 3+ hours (more than 25 consecutive cycles through 22:12Z):
  - `PRIORITY_CAPACITY product_target=11 product_active_verified=0 reserved_new=1`
  - `PRIORITY_RESERVATION requested=1 product_launched=0 held=1 discovery_complete=true launched=0`
  - `Dispatch path=floor complete: implementation_dispatched=0 ... processed=0/59`
- REST core had recovered by later cycles (`budget-priority ... rest=normal:565/5000`), but the floor throttle and held reservation stayed in place.
- Product (private managed repo) candidates in this window are mostly skipped before any outcome is recorded (`cross-cycle block:terminal_blocker_circuit`, `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked`, `(no wave slot spent)`). Roughly once an hour a single product attempt returns `dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=3` or `rc=2`. Tooling candidates (for example #37456, #37431, #37452) are listed first in the candidate preview, but none is processed.
- Worker utilisation: 0/18 for the whole window.

## Likely cause (verify before changing)

`_dispatch_priority_loop` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` (around lines 1350-1403) releases `held` only when discovery is complete, `product_unknown == 0` and **no product candidate remains** in the phase candidate file. Product candidates skipped by cross-cycle blocks produce no outcome but stay in the file, so `held` stays at 1. With `budget=1`, the remainder phase gets `phase_budget = 1 - held = 0`, so ordinary work is never assessed. This is a sibling of closed #31771 (the policy-held product candidate), seen here on the floor path. Confirm that by reproducing the case, not by assuming it.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `_dispatch_priority_loop` and `_dispatch_priority_reserved_pools`. Release a held slot when the product phase ends with no verified launch, no unknown outcome and only blocked or skipped product candidates. Do not wait for the candidate file to contain no product rows.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing.sh`: extend `assert_product_reservation_outcome` with one case: budget 1, reserved 1, every product candidate skipped by a cross-cycle block, and one eligible ordinary candidate. It should launch the ordinary candidate, and the existing `unknown` case must keep `held=1`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing.sh` passes, including the new case and both existing cases.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` is clean.
- After deploy, a degraded floor cycle with only blocked product candidates logs `held=0` and `processed>=1`.

## Out of scope

Do not change the floor throttle itself, REST-core admission or the terminal-blocker circuits.

<!-- aidevops:generator=agent-doc-simplification-gate cited_file=.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md threshold=500 -->

## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`
**Detected topic:** Cleanup and preservation contract
**Current size:** 500 lines

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md`

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Worker guidance

**Reference pattern:** `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md` (playbook for splits — covers orchestrator pattern, identity-key preservation, and PR body template).

**Precedent in this repo:** `issue-sync-helper.sh` + `issue-sync-lib.sh` (simple split) and `headless-runtime-lib.sh` + sub-libraries (complex split). For agent docs, see existing chapter-file splits in `.agents/reference/`.

**Expected CI gate overrides:** If this PR triggers a complexity regression from restructured files, apply the `complexity-bump-ok` label AND include a `## Complexity Bump Justification` section in the PR body citing scanner evidence. See the playbook section 4 (Known CI False-Positive Classes).

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md' | grep -c . | grep '^0$' >/dev/null` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)
- For reference corpora: `wc -l` total of chapter files >= original line count minus index overhead

### Confidence: medium

Automated scan flagged this file for review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

### Dispatch authority

This issue was created under verified maintainer authority and is ready for automated dispatch. No additional approval comment is required.

title: t18933: fix(screen-time): macOS screen time under-reports (inverted backlit spans, held pmset assertion, frozen snapshot)
body:
## Task


macOS profile README "Screen time" under-reports. For 2026-11-08 the README showed 8.0h (and interactive `profile-stats` 7.1h) while pmset display assertions now show 12.4h. Fix the four collection defects below so the macOS row measures display-on time correctly in both the launchd (no Full Disk Access) and interactive paths.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

macOS profile README "Screen time" under-reports. For 2026-11-08 the README showed 8.0h (and interactive `profile-stats` 7.1h) while pmset display assertions now show 12.4h. Fix the four collection defects below so the macOS row measures display-on time correctly in both the launchd (no Full Disk Access) and interactive paths.

## Why

Evidence (maintainer Mac, local TZ +0000):

1. **Backlit stream parsed inverted.** Each knowledgeC `/display/isBacklit` row is a completed span: the display held `ZVALUEINTEGER` from `ZSTARTDATE` to `ZENDDATE`; the row is written (`ZCREATIONDATE`) when the span ends. `parse_backlit_rows` treats `(ZCREATIONDATE, value)` as "state from now on", so every on-span is counted as off and vice versa. Per-day overlap with the pmset ∪ app-usage reference, 2026-10-22..11-05: current parse 0.0h overlap (it counts the complement; current + span ≈ 24h each day), span parse ≈ 100% overlap. Totals looked plausible because a 10-14h working day leaves 10-14h off.
2. **pmset misses the currently-held display assertion.** The parser reads only `Summary`/`Released` log lines. After the 2026-11-08 19:35 reboot no `Summary` lines were logged; the assertion appeared only when released at 2026-11-09 04:26 (duration 08:50:40). `pmset -g assertions` exposes the held assertion live (`pid 390(powerd): [...] 03:22:07 PreventUserIdleSystemSleep named: "Powerd - Prevent sleep while display is on"`).
3. **Snapshot never revisits a day.** The launchd snapshot recorded 2026-11-08 = 8.0h at 2026-11-09T01:40:31Z while the display was still on; replaying the parser at that instant reproduces 7.97h, now 12.38h. `cmd_snapshot` skips any already-recorded date, so the under-count is permanent and the README (history-preferred for the pmset proxy) shows it.
4. **Knowledge DB never unioned with pmset.** `collect()` uses pmset only when the knowledge DB is `unavailable`; a readable but gapped backlit stream (no rows ~2026-11-06..11-08 13:48) is never filled.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos.py`: read `ZSTARTDATE, ZENDDATE, ZVALUEINTEGER` for `/display/isBacklit`; parse to `(start, end, on)` spans; on-intervals are the value-1 spans; observations are span ends.
- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos_pmset.py`: add the live held display assertion from `pmset -g assertions` as `[now - held, now]`; fixture env `AIDEVOPS_PMSET_ASSERTIONS_FIXTURE`; when `AIDEVOPS_PMSET_FIXTURE` is set without it, no live read (deterministic tests). Keep unmatched `Display is turned on` notifications ignored (existing test intent).
- `.agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py` `collect()`: union the selected knowledge-DB intervals with pmset intervals when both are available; label the merged source.
- `.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh` `cmd_snapshot` + engine `revisable-dates`: re-record a date from the last 3 completed local days only when the recomputed value exceeds the recorded one (history is append-only; last row per date wins).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh`: backlit fixtures use span semantics; cover held assertion and snapshot revision.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean on changed shell files.
- On a Mac: `screen-time-helper.sh profile-stats` day/week no longer equal the display-off complement; launchd-equivalent run (`AIDEVOPS_KNOWLEDGE_DB=/nonexistent ... profile-stats`) day value after a fresh `snapshot` reflects the full pmset day.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos.py`
- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos_pmset.py`
- `.agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py`
- `.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh`

</details>

<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

Newly queued auto-dispatch work must pass its `Dispatch Readiness Contract (brief schema v2)`: complete write surface, hazards and compatibility, executable verification mapped to affected surfaces, and positive plus negative/regression acceptance criteria.

</details>

title: t18934: feat(screen-time): macOS input-activity row matching the Linux 5-minute input sampler
body:
## Task


Add a macOS "Input activity" row to the profile README "Work with AI" table, measured exactly like the Linux sampler: time counts from each keyboard/mouse input until 300s of idle (`linux-input-activity:idle-cutoff-300s` rule). Label the Linux row "Input activity (Linux)" (it already measures input, not screen-on time) and note whether the latest Linux sample saw desktop idle evidence or terminals only. Result: the maintainer's Mac README and contributors' Linux READMEs carry a like-for-like row for productivity comparison.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add a macOS "Input activity" row to the profile README "Work with AI" table, measured exactly like the Linux sampler: time counts from each keyboard/mouse input until 300s of idle (`linux-input-activity:idle-cutoff-300s` rule). Label the Linux row "Input activity (Linux)" (it already measures input, not screen-on time) and note whether the latest Linux sample saw desktop idle evidence or terminals only. Result: the maintainer's Mac README and contributors' Linux READMEs carry a like-for-like row for productivity comparison.

## Why

- macOS "Screen time (Mac)" is display-on time (knowledgeC backlit spans ∪ pmset display assertions, fixed in t18933 / GH#37492). Linux "Screen time (Linux)" is sampled human input with a 5-minute idle cut-off (`.agents/scripts/screen_time_linux_activity.py`, `DEFAULT_IDLE_SECONDS=300`). The two rows measure different things, so cross-platform comparison is misleading.
- macOS exposes system-wide input idle time permission-free: `ioreg -c IOHIDSystem -r -k HIDIdleTime -d 1` prints `"HIDIdleTime" = <ns>`. Verified on the maintainer Mac 2026-11-09: two reads 6s apart rose by 6.03e9, so the unit is nanoseconds.
- Linux evidence kinds are already recorded per sample (`state["evidence"]`, e.g. `gnome-idle-monitor`, `tty-atime`, `graphical-idle-unavailable`) but never shown, so a reader cannot tell whether a desktop was observed.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/screen_time_linux_activity.py`: make the collector name a parameter (default `linux-input-activity`) for `record_sample`, `record_line`, `source_name`, `unavailable`, `activity_collection`; keep file names and Linux behaviour unchanged.
2. New `.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos_input.py`: read the minimum `HIDIdleTime` from `ioreg` (fixture env `AIDEVOPS_HID_IDLE_FIXTURE` holding ioreg text), sample `last_input = now - idle_ns / 1e9` with evidence kind `hid-idle` (or `hid-idle-unavailable`), collector `macos-input-activity`, via `record_sample`; collection via `activity_collection`.
3. `.agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py`: `sample` on Darwin calls the macOS sampler (today it prints `no-sampler-needed:Darwin`); new `input-profile` command printing `profile_payload(<input collection>, None, now)` plus the collection `evidence` list; Linux input-profile uses `linux_collection`.
4. `.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh`: `input-stats` command → engine `input-profile`; update usage text.
5. `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh` `setup_screen_time_snapshot`: macOS LaunchAgent `sh.aidevops.screen-activity-sampler` running `screen-time-helper.sh sample` with `StartInterval` 60, mirroring the snapshot plist (Background, Nice 10, log `screen-activity-sampler.log`).
6. `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-data-lib.sh` (`_get_screen_time` pattern) + `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-render-lib.sh` (`_generate_screen_time_vars`, `_generate_work_with_ai_table`): on Darwin add an "Input activity (Mac)" row after "Screen time (Mac)" using the same formatting and sampling-began note; on Linux relabel the row "Input activity (Linux)" and append the latest-sample evidence (desktop idle vs terminals only).
7. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh`: fixture-driven macOS sample → input-profile hours and source `macos-input-activity:idle-cutoff-300s`.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh` passes; ShellCheck clean on changed shell files.
- On a Mac after `setup.sh --non-interactive`: `launchctl list | rg screen-activity-sampler` shows the job; `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/screen-activity-state.json` updates each minute; `screen-time-helper.sh input-stats` reports `macos-input-activity:idle-cutoff-300s` with `observed_since_epoch` set.
- Generated README shows "Screen time (Mac)" and "Input activity (Mac)" rows on macOS, "Input activity (Linux)" with an evidence note on Linux.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_linux_activity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_macos_input.py`
- `.agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py`
- `.agents/scripts/screen-time-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh`

title: Raise worktree cap to 1000, clean before throttling, report throughput throttles
body:
## Problem

Pulse dispatch fails closed when a repo has `AIDEVOPS_MAX_WORKTREES` (default 200) registered worktrees. On busy repos, real work was throttled while merged/stale worktrees waited for cleanup: one managed repo logged 629 `Live worktree count ... >= cap 200` refusals, and `cleanup_worktrees.log` repeatedly reported `capacity-stuck: gate closed, zero safe removals`.

The 200 value came from GH#18987 (PR #18990), whose body said "e.g. 200 max". It was an illustrative example, not a measured limit. The disk-capacity gate (`disk-capacity-lib.sh`, 5 GiB / 5% free) is the actual resource guard.

There is also no mechanism to surface requests that throttle throughput instead of fixing the root cause.

## Fix

1. Raise the default per-repo cap to 1000 as a runaway backstop. One shared default lives in `.agents/scripts/disk-capacity-lib.sh` (`aidevops_worktree_count_cap`).
2. Cleanup first: pressure cleanup starts at the lower of 80% of the cap and `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_CLEANUP_THRESHOLD` (default 150), so raising the cap never delays reclaiming redundant worktrees (`aidevops_worktree_cleanup_threshold`). Used by `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` and `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`.
3. Throughput-throttling policy: `.agents/reference/throughput-throttling-policy.md`, pointer in `.agents/AGENTS.md`. New `.agents/scripts/throttle-report-helper.sh report` files a report on this repo, labelled `throughput-throttle-report` + `needs-maintainer-review`, held from dispatch and assigned to the maintainer.
4. Trust plumbing: `shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` keeps NMR on throttle reports for trusted creators. `issue-triage-gate-reusable.yml` re-applies the hold and owner assignment from the body marker, because GitHub drops labels set by non-collaborators.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on changed scripts.
- `tests/test-pulse-dispatch-worktree-cap-cleanup.sh` passes.
- `tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`, `test-disk-capacity-lib.sh`, `test-gh-wrapper-nmr-normalization.sh` and `test-framework-issue-helper.sh` pass.
- `throttle-report-helper.sh report --dry-run ...` prints the expected labels, hold and body marker.
- `tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh` fails identically on unmodified `main` (fixture `fresh` worktree removed, count 8 vs expected 9). That failure predates this change.

title: Cut aidevops CI queue time: cancel superseded runs, consolidate small gates (no self-hosted runners)
body:
## Problem

aidevops CI queueing is the main limit on PR throughput. At one snapshot there were 37 queued and 73 in-progress runs, with an average queue wait of 440s (max 760s); Code Quality Analysis takes about 24 min per run. Jobs share the plan's concurrent-job limit on GitHub-hosted runners.

## Constraint (maintainer decision)

This public repo must not use self-hosted runners that belong to private projects. Self-hosted job logs are public and expose runner and machine names, which would identify private infrastructure. Stay on GitHub-hosted runners and reduce CI demand instead.

## Fix direction

1. Add `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` to PR-triggered workflows. About 39 non-reusable workflows currently lack `cancel-in-progress`, so superseded pushes keep occupying slots. Keep `cancel-in-progress: false` for push-to-main, release and publish workflows.
2. Consolidate small single-step lint gates into one job with steps. Candidates include `counter-stack-check`, `counter-monotonic`, `stat-portability-check`, `mktemp-portability-check`, `pipe-early-exit-check`, `shell-init-pattern-check`, `pulse-unbound-var-check`, `shellcheckrc-parity`, `workflow-cascade-lint`, `url-allowlist-check` and `task-id-collision-check`. Each job pays its own queue wait and runner start-up. Keep the existing required check names as job names, or update branch protection in the same change.
3. Tighten `paths:` filters so doc-only and planning-only PRs skip shell and quality gates.
4. Profile `code-quality.yml` (12 `runs-on`, ~24 min) and split it so only required checks gate merge; run heavy analysis post-merge.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/*.yml`: PR-triggered workflows listed above.
- `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`: record the concurrency and consolidation rule.

## Verification

- `rg -L "cancel-in-progress" .github/workflows -g "*.yml" -g "!*reusable*"` lists only push/release workflows.
- The required checks on main still report on a test PR.
- Median queue wait (created→started) over 24h drops; compare `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs` before and after.

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Worktree capacity cleanup depends on scarce REST reads and leaves merged trees registered
body:
## Problem

Worktree cleanup did not keep up with worker throughput. Before a supervised manual pass, one managed repo had 229 registered worktrees and another 196. A large share were stale: about 106 had MERGED PRs (62 older than 2 days), and 94 were detached. The async helper repeatedly logged `capacity-stuck: gate closed, zero safe removals`.

A manual `worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged` pass reduced the counts to 105 and 162. It removed directories but preserved many branches with `github evidence unavailable` (REST core budget exhausted). So capacity cleanup depends on GitHub REST reads that are scarce exactly when the pulse is busiest.

Observed related issues:

- One worker worktree was left half-torn-down (126 tracked files deleted) and is held by the safety guard.
- Peer evidence: about 48 trees are pinned by unfinished lifecycle runs of a long-lived interactive app session; they clear only on `full-loop-helper.sh finalize-receipt`, `complete`, or app exit.
- `tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh` fails on main: the fixture `fresh` worktree is removed, so the count is 8 instead of the expected 9.
- `--force-merged` produced no new `refs/aidevops/dirty-worktree-backups/` refs during a 100+ tree pass. Verify that the force path archives dirty trees before removal (`worktree-clean-lib.sh` `_skip_cleanup_for_dirty_state` ~531, `_clean_archive_dirty_worktree` ~1125).

## Fix direction

1. Prefer local merge proof (merged into `origin/main` by commit or patch-id, local PR cache) before GitHub reads in capacity mode.
2. Make the capacity pass reclaim MERGED-PR worktrees older than N hours automatically with archive-backed removal, without needing `--force-merged`.
3. Auto-release stale lifecycle pins when the owning PR is merged and the session is idle past a TTL.
4. Fix the test fixture expectation or the `fresh` handling regression.

## Files

`.agents/scripts/worktree-clean-lib.sh`, `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifecycle_status.py`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh`.

## Verification

- Registered worktree count stays below the cleanup threshold (150) on busy repos for 24h.
- No `capacity-stuck` lines in `cleanup_worktrees.log`.
- `test-worktree-capacity-recovery.sh` passes.

title: Pulse worker start latency 437-562s: move scanners off dispatch critical path
body:
## Problem

Pulse worker starts take 437–562s each. Pulse logs show `cache_prime`, `post_merge_scanner` and `release_repaired_brief_holds` repeatedly exceeding their stage timeouts. With a simultaneous-worker target of 20, only about 4 workers were active, even though capacity and provider accounts were available. Dispatch admission latency, not worker capacity, bounds throughput.

The GitHub REST core budget is also a limiter: about 345 of 5000 remained mid-window, and about 60% of the drop was unattributed by the local gh shim.

## Fix direction

1. Move `post_merge_scanner` and `release_repaired_brief_holds` out of the dispatch critical path, into an async stage with its own lock and budget.
2. Make `cache_prime` incremental: use ETag / `If-None-Match` conditional requests and GraphQL batching instead of per-issue REST.
3. Attribute all REST consumers in the shim so budget drains can be traced.
4. Dispatch admission should overlap with in-flight worker startup rather than serialising per worker.

## Files

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` stage scheduling, `.agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-instrument.sh`, the gh shim under `.agents/scripts/gh`.

## Verification

- `dispatch-timing-helper.sh` p50 per-worker start under 120s.
- Active workers reach the configured target when eligible issues exist.
- Rerun `dispatch-stage-instrument.sh` summaries before and after.

title: Privacy guard misses ordinary private repos (only mirror/local_only enumerated)
body:
## Problem

The public-write privacy guard misses ordinary private repositories. A worker-created issue on this public repo (#37478, since redacted) named a private managed repo in its body, and the gh shim allowed it.

`privacy_enumerate_private_slugs` (`.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh:221`) treats a repo as private only if `repos.json` gives it a non-empty `mirror_upstream` or `local_only: true`, or the slug is in `~/.aidevops/configs/privacy-guard-extra-slugs.txt`. A normal private GitHub repo with neither flag is not enumerated. The result also depends on each machine's local `repos.json`: the same repo can be protected on one maintainer's machine and unprotected on another's worker host.

## Reproducer

1. In `repos.json`, register a private GitHub repo with no `mirror_upstream` or `local_only` flag, and keep it out of the extra-slugs file.
2. Run `gh issue create --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --title test --body "<that repo's basename> candidates"` with `--dry-run` or against a fixture repo.
3. Observed: `[privacy-scan][ALLOW]`. Expected: `[privacy-scan][BLOCK]`.

## Fix direction

1. **r914 files duplicate trust-workflow issues from stale local checkouts.** `check-workflows-helper.sh` is deliberately a no-network local audit (`.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh:663-666`). When a canonical checkout is behind `origin/main`, it reports `NO-WORKFLOW` for a caller already merged on the remote, and says so in its own note (`"local evidence; main is 4 commit(s) behind origin/main"`, `evidence.freshness: "behind"`). `_trust_install_one` (`.agents/scripts/repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh:736-808`) treats that as authoritative, creates the tracking issue (`:779`), and then the sync helper "made no PR". title: pulse: stalled worker draft checkpoints pause forever once every runner has tried the head; no maintainer resume route
body:
## What

A worker draft checkpoint that stalls with no recorded blocker can stay paused indefinitely. This happens with stall-class releases such as `stale_assignment_reset`, and with `worker_complete` released by a continuation session while the draft is still open. Once every runner in the fleet has tried the head, nothing continues it automatically. A maintainer also has no supported "continue" approval for these releases. The remaining exits all lose either time or work: mark ready (the work is incomplete), push a "corrected" commit (there is nothing to correct), or close the draft (discards the preserved checkpoint).

## Evidence (managed `<webapp>` repo, 2026-11-10 01:10Z, runners on v3.39.150 and v3.39.153)

- 9 substantive worker drafts (325–13,779 added lines, several already published to beta) have each been held for 2–3 days by `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION`. Their award issues stay `status:available` but never dispatch (`WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT ... ordinary redispatch is blocked`). The pulse logs `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS` every cycle on both Linux runners.
- Re-arm rule: `_pcc_dispatch_stalled` in `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:1579-1589` re-arms only when `_pcc_runner_tried_head` (`:1372`) is false for the current runner. With two or three runners, every runner has tried the head within about a day. After that the pause is permanent, even though the per-PR fuse (`AIDEVOPS_PCC_MAX_PR_RELEASES`, 6) hasn't been reached.
- The only untried runner, a macOS runner, couldn't take its re-arm: its dispatch fails closed with `Live worktree count 228 >= cap 200 ... dispatch remains fail-closed`. A single runner's local capacity therefore decides whether shared work continues.
- Approval route: `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template` refuses these releases with `release <id> is not a trusted blocked/clean/worker_complete release closing attempt:<id> with its poster's ready lease; dispatch-approved would reject this approval, so none was generated`. It did so for two continuation-session `worker_complete` releases. Stall-class releases (`stale_assignment_reset`) are outside the accepted set by design (`reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`, "Approving a corrected released checkpoint").
- The `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` comment offers only mark-ready, push or close, so a write-authorised owner can't resume the preserved head.

## How

1. **Automatic continuation, bounded:** once every runner has tried the head, re-arm one exact-head continuation per fresh window (for example `AIDEVOPS_PCC_ATTENTION_REARM_SECONDS`, doubling for each re-arm of the same head) instead of pausing permanently. Pick the runner through the normal fenced claim. Keep the per-PR fuse (`_PCC_MAX_PR_RELEASES`) as the hard stop, and keep `_pcc_self_capability_release` and runner-capability exclusions. Files: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` (`_pcc_dispatch_stalled`, `_pcc_runner_tried_head`), plus the matching negative-cache boundary in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:303/433` so cached hints expire at the new re-arm time.
2. **Maintainer resume route:** let `approval-template` and `dispatch-approved` accept stall-class releases (`stale_assignment_reset`, stall/timeout, `worker_ownership_lost`, `worker_noop_zero_output`, `worker_incomplete_exit`). Also accept continuation-session `clean`/`worker_complete` releases whose poster is a trusted runner. Keep every existing binding: exact head/ref, release ID, brief SHA-256, 24h expiry, current permissions, coordination history, fenced claim. Add the generated command to the `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` text, as `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` already does.
3. Update `reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md` ("Non-blocked releases with an open draft") to describe the new re-arm schedule and the resume route.

## Acceptance

- In a fixture where every runner has tried the head and no fuse is reached, a later re-arm window logs `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARMED` and launches exactly one exact-head continuation. The per-PR fuse still stops it.
- `approval-template` produces a valid line for a `stale_assignment_reset` release and for a continuation-session `worker_complete` release. `dispatch-approved` accepts the line, and rejects it after a head, brief or permission change.
- Existing tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` and `test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` still pass.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** as a runner account, `tail -n 20000 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep -ao 'STALLED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS: PR #[0-9]*' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head`. Then, for one of those PRs: `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh approval-template OWNER/REPO PR ISSUE RELEASE_ID attempt:ID`, using the newest `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment ID and the last lease attempt.

**Actual output:** the same PRs repeat every cycle for 2–3 days with no `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_REARMED`. `approval-template` exits 1 with `is not a trusted blocked/clean/worker_complete release ... none was generated`.

**Expected:** the stalled head is continued automatically on a bounded schedule. When a maintainer wants it sooner, `approval-template` produces an approval line.

  - Receipt: one issue comment whose body starts `<!-- aidevops:already-satisfied-completion:v1 -->\n`, followed on line 2 by JSON: `schema` (1), `repository`, `issue`, `attempt_id`, `attempt_started_at` (must equal `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_ID` / `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_STARTED_AT`), `disposition` (`already_satisfied` | `premise_falsified`), `rationale` (string, ≥20 chars), `path` (repo-relative, no `.`/`..` segments), `blob` (40-hex), and `evidence_pr` (positive int; required for `already_satisfied`).

    - Comment `created_at` ≥ attempt start; `updated_at` ≤ issue `closed_at`; `html_url` matches the issue.

    - The live default branch has `path` at `blob`: after `_hrw_pr_less_worktree_clean` (it fetches the live default tip into `FETCH_HEAD`), `git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD:<path>` equals `blob`.

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` Outcome A (line ~32), and the already-satisfied exception in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` (Mandatory behavior 6 and the pre-exit self-check). Tell workers to post this receipt (exact format) before closing, and say a bare marker is not credited.

### Files Scope

- Existing review-triage cases in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh` (run via `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Credit a headless worker that correctly closes an already-satisfied or premise-falsified issue without a PR, using an evidence-bound receipt the runtime verifies independently. Today such a run is recorded `worker_noop_zero_output` even when the close is correct.

## Why (evidence)

- GH#37510 / PR #37512 documented the no-PR terminal exception: workers verify on the live remote default branch, post an evidence comment, close the issue, keep the branch clean, and emit the completion marker. That stops the wasted continuation (`premature_exit` → exit 85 `worker_ownership_lost`).
- The run is still not credited. `_run_result_terminal_completion_confirmed` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh:205-210`) accepts the bare marker. But `_hrw_finish_success_run` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:1845-1856` calls `_worker_produced_output` unless `_hrw_terminal_objective_complete` passes, and a clean zero-commit branch classifies as `noop` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-output.sh:234-246`). The result is `_report_failure_to_fast_fail worker_noop_zero_output`, a failure metric for a correct outcome.
- `_hrw_pr_less_terminal_complete` (`headless-runtime-worker.sh:784-840`) has no predicate for this shape. `_hrw_already_delivered_terminal_complete` (`:950-987`) needs a merged PR whose `closingIssuesReferences` names *this* issue. A duplicate rollout issue was satisfied by a PR that closed the *earlier* issue, and its body has no `### Files Scope`, so the scoped-delivery path fails as well.
- Found by CodeRabbit on PR #37512 (review thread on `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md:143`): "do not treat the `TASK_COMPLETE` marker alone as sufficient". The framework deliberately refuses self-attested PR-less closes. Every existing predicate binds to independent forge evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- A closed issue with a valid receipt, a clean branch, no pushed branch and no PR classifies as success (`_hrw_terminal_objective_complete` returns 0), not `worker_noop`.
- Each of these is rejected with a distinct `_HRW_PR_LESS_REJECTION`:
  - A missing, duplicated, stale (created before attempt start), or edited-after-close receipt.
  - A closer/author mismatch.
  - A path not named in the issue body.
  - A blob that differs from the live default.
  - `already_satisfied` without a merged evidence PR that touched the path.
- Review-feedback issues are unaffected.
- Existing completion tests still pass.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`. Add focused accept/reject cases next to the review-triage cases; this is a trust-boundary predicate, so coverage is required.
