title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #28838 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #28838

**Parent issue:** #28838 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,needs-consolidation,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> Sources are inlined below unless explicitly listed as omitted. Fetch omitted references before consolidating.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #28838 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`
   That marker must be a line by itself, exactly as shown (no extra text, no trailing whitespace); the dispatch gate refuses consolidated successors without it. Put any further lineage (for example "#28838 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 28838 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent.** Run all four commands below for #28838, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing). Do not close this consolidation task until every parent's handoff is complete:

```bash
gh issue comment 28838 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 28838 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 28838 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 28838 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #28838 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #28838.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Checkpoint recovery is never an unconditional requirement** (GH#35871). Name a checkpoint commit or branch as binding only after verifying it is reachable from a remote ref (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<sha>`), recording the full SHA and ref. Otherwise write: "Best-effort recovery: reuse if reachable; the functional spec is the source of truth; re-implement if unrecoverable." Never forbid re-implementing work that exists only as local commits on one runner.

Lineage: #28838 was previously consolidated by #33327 into #33448 (delivered by merged PR #33449, canary extraction). The file has since regrown past the limit, so this successor replaces that closed thread for the current regrowth.

## What

## Why

## How

Reference pattern: `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md` (playbook: identity-key preservation, CI false-positives, PR body template). ## Agent doc simplification (automated scan)

**File:** `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`
**Detected topic:** Corrected blocked checkpoint recovery
**Current size:** 500 lines

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`

### Classify before acting

**First, determine the file type** — the correct action depends on whether this is an instruction doc or a reference corpus:

- **Instruction doc** (agent rules, workflows, decision trees, operational procedures): Tighten prose, reorder by importance, split if multiple concerns. Follow guidance below.
- **Reference corpus** (SKILL.md, domain knowledge base, textbook-style content with self-contained sections): Do NOT compress content. Instead, split into chapter files with a slim index. See `tools/code-review/code-simplifier.md` "Reference corpora" classification (GH#6432).

### For instruction docs — proposed action

Tighten and restructure this agent doc. Follow `tools/build-agent/build-agent.md` guidance. Key principles:

1. **Preserve all institutional knowledge** — every verbose rule exists because something broke without it. Do not remove task IDs, incident references, error statistics, or decision rationale. Compress prose, not knowledge.
2. **Order by importance** — most critical instructions first (primacy effect: LLMs weight earlier context more heavily). Security rules, core workflow, then edge cases.
3. **Split if needed** — if the file covers multiple distinct concerns, extract sub-docs with a parent index. Use progressive disclosure (pointers, not inline content).
4. **Use search patterns, not line numbers** — any `file:line_number` references to other files go stale on every edit. Use `rg "pattern"` or section heading references instead.

### For reference corpora — proposed action

1. **Extract each major section** into its own file (e.g., `01-introduction.md`, `02-fundamentals.md`)
2. **Replace the original with a slim index** (~100-200 lines) — table of contents with one-line descriptions and file pointers
3. **Zero content loss** — every line moves to a chapter file, nothing is deleted or compressed
4. **Reconcile existing chapter files** — if partial splits already exist, deduplicate and keep the most complete version

### Worker guidance

**Reference pattern:** `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md` (playbook for splits — covers orchestrator pattern, identity-key preservation, and PR body template).

**Precedent in this repo:** `issue-sync-helper.sh` + `issue-sync-lib.sh` (simple split) and `headless-runtime-lib.sh` + sub-libraries (complex split). For agent docs, see existing chapter-file splits in `.agents/reference/`.

**Expected CI gate overrides:** If this PR triggers a complexity regression from restructured files, apply the `complexity-bump-ok` label AND include a `## Complexity Bump Justification` section in the PR body citing scanner evidence. See the playbook section 4 (Known CI False-Positive Classes).

### Verification

- Content preservation: all code blocks, URLs, task ID references (`tNNN`, `GH#NNN`), and command examples must be present before and after
- No broken internal links or references
- Agent behaviour unchanged (test with a representative query if possible)
- Qlty smells resolved for the target file: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --all 2>&1 | grep '.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md' | grep -c . | grep '^0$' >/dev/null` (report `SKIP` if Qlty is unavailable, not `FAIL`)

Automated scan flagged this file for review. The best simplification strategy requires human judgment — some files are appropriately structured already. Reference corpora (SKILL.md, domain knowledge bases) need restructuring into chapters, not content reduction.

title: t18937: shared-model-tier: warn when custom routing tiers list interactive-only providers (claudecli, cursor)
body:
## Task


When a custom model routing table lists a model whose provider only works interactively (`claudecli/*` or `cursor/*`), aidevops warns instead of staying silent:

1. `model_tier_candidates` prints one stderr warning per process naming each such tier and model. It says headless workers cannot use them and will fall through to the next candidate.
2. `aidevops doctor` reports the same finding in its model routing override check.

Resolution behaviour does not change. The same candidates are returned in the same order, so this is visibility only.

## Done when

- [ ] With a custom table listing `claudecli/*` or `cursor/*` in any tier, `model_tier_candidates` writes exactly one interactive-only warning to stderr per process, naming each `tier: model`
- [ ] `aidevops doctor` (via `doctor-helper.sh`) reports the same interactive-only finding
- [ ] Regression: candidate stdout and its order are unchanged, `google/*` entries do not trigger the warning, and the framework default table emits no warning
- [ ] Regression: `claudecli` is still not a known provider for headless availability
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-overlay.sh` passes and `shellcheck` is clean on both edited files

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh:110-161` — add `model_routing_custom_table_interactive_only_findings` and a warn-once sibling. Call it from `model_tier_candidates` next to the existing call at line 182
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/doctor-helper.sh:328-355` — report the new findings after the structural check passes

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `model_tier_candidates` (`shared-model-tier.sh:167`) is the only runtime caller of the validators. `doctor-helper.sh:346` calls `model_routing_custom_table_validation_findings` directly. `rg -n "model_routing_custom_table_validation_findings|model_routing_warn_invalid_custom_table" .agents` finds only those two files
- **Writers/mutation paths:** No writer changes. The routing table is written only by users at `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/configs/model-routing-table.json` or `AIDEVOPS_MODEL_ROUTING_TABLE` (`model_routing_table_path`, `shared-model-tier.sh:80-100`). The new function only reads it with `jq -r`. The only new mutable state is the in-process once-flag variable `_MODEL_ROUTING_INTERACTIVE_ONLY_WARNING_EMITTED`
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-overlay.sh` uses `AIDEVOPS_MODEL_ROUTING_TABLE` custom tables and must keep passing. No existing test pins the warning text (`rg -ln "has invalid tiers" .agents/scripts/tests` returns nothing)
- **Schemas/config:** The routing table schema (`.agents/configs/model-routing-table.json`) is unchanged
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`. There are no generated mirrors
- **Migrations/backfills:** None required. The routing table schema and stored data are unchanged, and the warning is computed on every read from the current table, so existing user tables need no backfill. Users clear the warning by editing their own table (remove `claudecli/*`/`cursor/*` or use `anthropic/*`)
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Rollback is a plain `git revert` of the commit, then `setup.sh --non-interactive` to redeploy. No files, caches or labels are created, so there is nothing to clean up. The model-availability SQLite cache is not touched

### Implementation Steps

1. In `shared-model-tier.sh`, add the findings function right after `model_routing_custom_table_validation_findings`. Use the same guard (skip when the custom table is empty or equals the framework table, and skip when jq is missing). Emit one line per offending entry:

```bash
#######################################
# Print custom-table entries whose provider is interactive-only. Headless
# workers never start these local proxies (index.mjs isHeadless gate) and
# claudecli models are registered with tool_call:false, so workers fall
# through to the next candidate. `google` is deliberately excluded: google/*
# is also a native API-key provider.
#######################################
model_routing_custom_table_interactive_only_findings() {
	local custom_table="$1"
	local framework_table="$2"
	[[ -n "$custom_table" && "$custom_table" != "$framework_table" ]] || return 0
	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
	jq -r '
		(.tiers // {}) | to_entries[]
		| select((.value | type) == "object" and (.value.models | type) == "array")
		| .key as $tier
		| .value.models[] | select(type == "string")
		| select(test("^(claudecli|cursor)/"))
		| "\($tier): \(.)"
	' "$custom_table" 2>/dev/null || true
	return 0
}
```

2. Add `model_routing_warn_interactive_only_providers`, modelled on `model_routing_warn_invalid_custom_table` (lines 150-161). Give it its own once-flag `_MODEL_ROUTING_INTERACTIVE_ONLY_WARNING_EMITTED`. Message: `WARNING: custom model routing table lists interactive-only providers; headless workers cannot use them and fall through to the next candidate (use anthropic/* via the OAuth pool for Claude subscriptions): <findings joined by "; ">`. Call it immediately after line 182, inside the same `command -v jq` block.
3. In `doctor-helper.sh`, after the structural `findings` check (line 346-351) and before `print_success`, call the new findings function (guard with `declare -F` like lines 333-337). If it returns anything, `print_warning "Model routing override: interactive-only providers listed (headless workers skip them): ..."` and set `CONFLICTS_FOUND=1`.
4. Run `shellcheck` on both files.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** None. A pure read of one JSON file per call
- **Migration/rollback:** None. A plain revert works
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Candidate output stays the same. Only new stderr text is added, and it goes out at most once per process. Callers that capture stdout (`$(model_tier_candidates ...)`) are unaffected because the warning goes to stderr, the same as the existing warning at line 159
- **Idempotency/retry:** The once-flag stops the same process repeating the warning
- **Partial failure/recovery:** A jq error is swallowed (`|| true`) and resolution still succeeds. A malformed table is already reported by the structural validator

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `model_tier_candidates` in `shared-model-tier.sh`
- **Current line count:** about 45 lines (threshold 100)
- **Estimated growth:** +1 line
- **Projected post-change:** about 46 lines (46%)
- **Action required:** None

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp); printf '%s\n' '{"tiers":{"simple":{"models":["claudecli/claude-haiku-5-5","anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5"]}}}' > "$tmp"
AIDEVOPS_MODEL_ROUTING_TABLE="$tmp" bash -c 'source .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh; model_tier_candidates simple' # stdout: both models, order unchanged; stderr: one interactive-only warning naming simple: claudecli/claude-haiku-5-5
AIDEVOPS_MODEL_ROUTING_TABLE="$tmp" .agents/scripts/doctor-helper.sh # routing section prints the interactive-only warning
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-model-routing-overlay.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh .agents/scripts/doctor-helper.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** The first command proves the warning appears and output does not change. The second proves doctor reports it. The overlay test proves existing custom-table inheritance still works. ShellCheck covers both edited files
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required. Two leaf helpers, no shared contract change

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** Do not filter or reorder candidates. Do not mark `claudecli` or `cursor` as known or available in `model-availability-helper.sh` or `model-availability-probe-lib.sh`. Do not touch the OpenCode plugin or OAuth pool code.

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (maintainer)

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/doctor-helper.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch `shared-model-tier.sh` or `doctor-helper.sh` in the last 48h (latest: `3c544c30e6` GH#36714). Search for related issues: none

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-10
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer review session)
- **Conversation context:** Follow-up from the maintainer review of #37509 (declined) and PR #37511 (closed). A contributor's custom routing table sent the `simple` and `standard` worker tiers to `claudecli/*`. Workers silently fell through to another provider, and nothing warned that the table was unusable in headless sessions.

## What

When a custom model routing table lists a model whose provider only works interactively (`claudecli/*` or `cursor/*`), aidevops warns instead of staying silent:

1. `model_tier_candidates` prints one stderr warning per process naming each such tier and model. It says headless workers cannot use them and will fall through to the next candidate.
2. `aidevops doctor` reports the same finding in its model routing override check.

Resolution behaviour does not change. The same candidates are returned in the same order, so this is visibility only.

## Why

- `claudecli/*` is the interactive Claude CLI transport. Headless sessions never start its proxy (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs:607`, rationale at `proxy-lifecycle.mjs:39-43`, #21951), and its models are registered with `tool_call: false` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs:61-70`). `cursor` is a lazy-started local proxy in the same dispatch table (`index.mjs:593-597`) and is also skipped in headless sessions.
- The supported Claude subscription route for workers is `anthropic/*` through the OAuth pool. That is the framework default (`.agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh:205-207`).
- Today `model_routing_custom_table_validation_findings` (`shared-model-tier.sh:113-145`) checks only structure, so this misconfiguration is invisible. In #37509 it led to a source patch that would have marked `claudecli` as healthy for workers. Surfacing it at the point of configuration prevents that.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The pattern is a sibling of an existing warn-once validator, and the behaviour and wording are decided. The worker still has to write the jq filter and the doctor wiring, so this is not a verbatim contract.

## Context & Decisions

- Warn only, not filter. Interactive users may still list these providers on purpose, and resolution already falls through to the next candidate, so a warning fixes the visibility gap without changing behaviour.
- `google` is excluded because `google/*` is also a native API-key provider. Flagging it would cause false positives.
- Ruled out: making `claudecli` look available to the headless resolver (PR #37511, closed). Workers would be routed to a transport that is not started in headless sessions and has no tool calling.

- `.agents/scripts/shared-model-tier.sh:110-211` — validators and `model_tier_candidates`
- `.agents/scripts/doctor-helper.sh:328-355` — routing override check
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs:593-616` — proxy dispatch table and headless gate (read-only context)

body:
## Task


Make the pulse dead-stamp reaper (`interactive-session-helper.sh reap-dead-stamps`) reach every interactive claim stamp, not only the first `AIDEVOPS_DEAD_STAMP_REAP_LIMIT` (default 100) in glob order. Persist a rotation cursor so each bounded cycle resumes after the last examined stamp and wraps around.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`
  - Extract the per-stamp body of the `_isc_scan_dead_stamps_phase` loop into a helper. This keeps the coordinator under the 100-line function gate.
  - When `stamp_limit > 0`, read a cursor (basename of the last examined stamp) from `${CLAIM_STAMP_DIR}/.reap-cursor`. Examine stamps sorted after the cursor first, then wrap to the start. Stop at the limit.
  - When the cap stops the scan, write the last examined basename. When a full pass completes under the cap, remove the cursor.
  - Cursor I/O failures are non-fatal: an unreadable cursor restarts from the beginning, the previous behaviour. The dotfile is invisible to the `*.json` enumerators (`:482`, `interactive-session-helper-commands.sh:919`).
  - Unbounded calls (`scan-stale`, `stamp_limit=0`) ignore and never write the cursor.
  - Safety gates (hostname, PID/argv, recoverable progress, lockdown, lookup failure) are unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh`

### Reference pattern

- Existing Test 18 in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh:564-578` (per-cycle cap).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the pulse dead-stamp reaper (`interactive-session-helper.sh reap-dead-stamps`) reach every interactive claim stamp, not only the first `AIDEVOPS_DEAD_STAMP_REAP_LIMIT` (default 100) in glob order. Persist a rotation cursor so each bounded cycle resumes after the last examined stamp and wraps around.

## Why (evidence)

- `_isc_scan_dead_stamps_phase` (`.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh:468-554`) iterates `"$CLAIM_STAMP_DIR"/*.json` in sorted order and `break`s after `stamp_limit` stamps (`:484-486`). `_isc_cmd_reap_dead_stamps` (`:559-568`) passes the 100 cap on every pulse cycle (GH#28211 added the cap to bound per-cycle cost).
- With more than 100 stamps, the same first 100 are examined every cycle and the rest never are. Observed locally: 394 stamps across 5 owner prefixes. The first 100 cover two owners entirely and 30 of 256 stamps of a third. The remaining 294 stamps (including every stamp for the framework repository's owner after the first 30, and all of a fourth owner's 67) are never reaped.
- Effect on dispatch: dead claims stay self-assigned and block `auto-dispatch` work with `dedup_active_claim_unverified`. Example: two `origin:interactive` + `status:claimed` issues claimed 2026-10-29 by an owner PID that no longer exists, with the claim worktree removed. They were blocked every cycle for 12 days, while the pulse ran 0 of 20 worker slots. The stampless pass (`pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:948-1035`) skips them because a stamp exists (`:994-998`), so only the reaper can release them.
- The reaper logs `No releasable stale claims for 7 dead stamp(s)` every cycle, which reads as healthy while about 75% of stamps go unexamined.

## Acceptance criteria

- With limit N and M > N dead releasable stamps, every stamp is examined within ceil(M/N) consecutive calls.
- The per-cycle cap still holds: Test 18 passes unchanged.
- `scan-stale` (unbounded) behaviour is unchanged.
- No new GitHub API calls per cycle.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh`. Extend Test 18 with a second call that must release the stamp after the cursor. A fairness regression fails silently in production, so this case is the cheapest proof.
- After deploy: the reaper summary shows stamps beyond the first 100 being examined, and the two 12-day-old dead claims release within 4 cycles.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below, fetching any explicitly omitted sources first.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.

Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.

Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.

Put any further lineage (for example "#37375 itself superseded #M") on a separate line, and add one exact marker line per additional superseded issue.

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the parent body (inlined or explicitly fetched) verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --parent 37375 \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
# Repeat --parent for each additional superseded issue number.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks the exact marker line for every `--parent`, verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close every superseded parent.** Run all four commands below for #37375, then repeat them for every additional issue passed as `--parent` in step 3, substituting that issue number in every command (including dependency repointing). Do not close this consolidation task until every parent's handoff is complete:

```bash
gh issue comment 37375 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 37375 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 37375 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
# Repoint open dependants' blockedBy edges and Blocked-by lines at the successor (GH#35130):
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-repoint-helper.sh repoint "marcusquinn/aidevops" 37375 $NEW_NUM
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #37375 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- Read only explicitly omitted source references when the packet size limit prevents inlining them; otherwise do NOT re-read #37375.

The PR #37359 diagnosis also reported zero sessions and a dead ancillary owner. This does not establish a provider crash. Both events predate activation of PR #37359's unrelated claim-release correction; do not claim a post-update recurrence without fresh evidence.

A false `worker_noop_zero_output` misroutes recovery (infrastructure cooldown instead of a real failure cause), while a genuine unperformed review response leaves review threads unanswered. The outcome must be truthful either way.

Publication history (from the parent): a prior issue-create attempt timed out. A subsequent authoritative latest-30-issues read at approximately 15:02 UTC covered creation times 12:07:18–14:56:30 UTC and confirmed that no issue with this exact title had been created during the attempted publication interval. An earlier search-index miss alone was not used as absence evidence.

## How

### 1. Gather evidence first

- Start with `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 24h --no-pr-check --json` and `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr` for the exact two PRs (#37359, #37364), then inspect only the named attempt evidence and deployed entry points.
- The two cited attempt records live on another runner host (per @marcusquinn); a runner that cannot read them must say so with evidence rather than infer.
- Per @marcusquinn, read the private worker log for each attempt (local only): check the `[exit-trap] … session_count=` line, `db_merged` / `db_merge_failed`, and whether any reply or `mark-complete` / `mark-blocked` was posted on either PR between the attempt and merge.

### 2. Public timeline (per @marcusquinn)

| PR | First review thread (CodeRabbit) | Attempt epoch | Merged |
|----|----------------------------------|---------------|--------|
| #37359 | 2026-11-09T13:35:54Z (1 thread) | 1794231671 = 13:41:11Z | 14:05:53Z |
| #37364 | 2026-11-09T13:53:16Z (2 threads) | 1794233267 = 14:07:47Z | 14:30:46Z |

Every thread is now resolved, but each was created before its attempt and the PR was still open at attempt time. So **legitimate no-work (PR merged or nothing actionable) is unlikely** for both. The question becomes "unperformed response" versus "classification defect".

### 3. Classification path on current main (line numbers verified against `origin/main` at consolidation time)

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` `classify_worker_exit` (starts line 1084; zero-output branch ~1116-1131) returns `worker_noop_zero_output` for wait-status 0 when `_hrff_attempt_activity_count` (line 84, ~84-106) is 0. That count is assistant messages and parts since `_WORKER_START_EPOCH_MS`. The EXIT trap (~1931-1950) records it through `_hrff_record_exit_metric` (line 1740, ~1740-1766) with `classification_source=exit_trap`.
- The normal finish path clears the trap in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` `_hrw_finish_cleanup` (~1829). An exit_trap record with status 0 means that path did not run. Launch did start: otherwise the reason would be `worker_runtime_not_invoked`.

### 4. What current code already does (per @marcusquinn)

- `.agents/scripts/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:991-1036` (`_prrts_is_zero_session_infrastructure_outcome`, `_prrts_infrastructure_retry_status`): an outcome matching the dispatch with `worker_noop_zero_output` and `session_count=0` is classified as infrastructure failure, excluded from remediation escalation, and retried after a short cooldown under a bounded circuit breaker. This already meets "genuine unperformed work remains failed with bounded recovery" for real zero-output runs.

### 5. Local recurrence evidence from one runner host (per @marcusquinn, counts only)

- Lifetime review-response exit-trap records with `worker_noop_zero_output session_count=0`: 6, all well before this issue's observation date.
- `[lifecycle] db_merge_failed` in the same log: 26 of roughly 600 finalized runs. None of the 6 zero-output records falls inside the merge-failure cluster, so merge failure does not explain them on that host.

### 6. Candidate classification defect to verify (unproven for the two cited attempts)

Per @marcusquinn:

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh:577-593` (`_invoke_opencode_finalize_data`) calls `_finalize_isolated_runtime_data` on every normal return from the runtime.
2. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:199-237` (`_finalize_isolated_runtime_data`) merges the isolated DB into the shared DB, or discards it for ephemeral roles (`_headless_run_is_ephemeral`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh:60-68`: private workload, triage, model-replay), then sets `_WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH=""` (line 230).
3. The exit trap runs later. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` `classify_worker_exit` (exit status 0, ~1121-1134) and the exit-trap session count for the comment (~1942-1950) fall back to the shared DB when `_WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH` is empty.
4. So when the isolated DB was discarded (ephemeral role) or its merge failed (preserved elsewhere), `_hrff_attempt_activity_count` reads 0 from the shared DB even if the attempt produced assistant output. That yields a false `worker_noop_zero_output`.

### 7. Suggested minimal correction (only if step 6 reproduces)

- Per @marcusquinn: snapshot the attempt activity count from the isolated DB inside `_finalize_isolated_runtime_data`, before merge or discard (for example a global `_WORKER_ATTEMPT_ACTIVITY_COUNT`), and have `classify_worker_exit` and the exit-trap session count prefer that snapshot when `_WORKER_ISOLATED_DB_PATH` is empty.
- Alternative per @marcusquinn's earlier note: if `db_merge_failed` appears, count against the preserved DB in `classify_worker_exit`, or classify as `worker_incomplete_exit` rather than `worker_noop_zero_output`.
- Extend the existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-exit-classifier.sh` cases (t3050 block, around lines 165-200) with one discarded-isolated-DB case. No new runner.
- If the classifier path does not reproduce, document that current code (scanner lines in step 4) already gives bounded recovery and close without speculative changes.

### Reference history

Reference historical fixes #30153 (continued-session false positive), #30817 (infrastructure no-op cooldown), and #36597 (checkpoint release). Do not blindly reapply them.

Read-only references (not in the write surface): `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-launch.sh`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the two attempts is classified, with evidence, as legitimate no-work, unperformed review response, or classification defect (or explicitly recorded as unreadable from the diagnosing runner).
- [ ] Legitimate no-work receives a truthful explicit outcome; genuine unperformed work remains failed with an actionable cause and bounded recovery.

  - `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-review-thread-response-scanner-dispatch.sh`

- [ ] Keep raw private excerpts, credentials and local/private paths out of public comments.

title: t18939: fix(privacy-guard): enumeration expires known-public repos after 10 minutes and blocks dispatch claim comments
body:
## Task


Stop the public-write privacy guard from treating known-public repositories as private ten minutes after their last visibility probe. `privacy_enumerate_private_slugs` must honour a cached public observation for a long enumeration window (default 7 days, `PRIVACY_ENUM_PUBLIC_TTL`), not the 10-minute push-probe TTL. Unknown visibility (no cache entry) still fails closed for pulse-enabled repos, as GH#37508 intended.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`
  - Add `PRIVACY_ENUM_PUBLIC_TTL="${PRIVACY_ENUM_PUBLIC_TTL:-604800}"` next to `PRIVACY_CACHE_TTL`, with a comment: enumeration needs last-known visibility, not push-time freshness.
  - Pass it as the enumeration `ttl` (`:253`). Update the comment block (`:240-244`).
  - Private entries stay protected after expiry, and no-entry pulse repos still fail closed (unchanged).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`: add cases.
  - A public entry older than `PRIVACY_CACHE_TTL` but younger than `PRIVACY_ENUM_PUBLIC_TTL` is not enumerated.
  - A public entry older than `PRIVACY_ENUM_PUBLIC_TTL` is enumerated (fail closed).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`

### Reference pattern

- Existing GH#37508 cases in `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh` and `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard-shim.sh`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Stop the public-write privacy guard from treating known-public repositories as private ten minutes after their last visibility probe. `privacy_enumerate_private_slugs` must honour a cached public observation for a long enumeration window (default 7 days, `PRIVACY_ENUM_PUBLIC_TTL`), not the 10-minute push-probe TTL. Unknown visibility (no cache entry) still fails closed for pulse-enabled repos, as GH#37508 intended.

## Why (evidence)

- GH#37508 / PR #37513 (merged 2026-11-10 02:12Z, hot-deployed) added cached visibility to `privacy_enumerate_private_slugs` (`.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh:240-268`). It nulls any public cache entry older than `PRIVACY_CACHE_TTL` (600 s, `:40`; expiry at `:258`), and a null entry on a pulse-enabled repo is enumerated as private (`:262`). Nothing on the enumeration path refreshes the cache: only a push or write *target* probe does (`privacy_is_target_public`, `:85-162`).
- Result: every pulse-enabled public repo becomes "private" ten minutes after its last probe. Local snapshot: of 68 pulse-enabled repos, 14 public entries were expired and enumerated as private; only 2 fresh-public repos were excluded.
- The bare-basename scan (`privacy_scan_bare_basenames`, `:561-606`) then blocks any public write that mentions those basenames. The framework signature footer links the public site `aidevops.sh`, which is also the basename of a public pulse-enabled repo, and the framework repo's basename `aidevops` appears in most bodies.
- Impact since deploy: `pulse.log` shows 63 `[privacy-scan][BLOCK]` lines, all on public targets ("aidevops.sh (basename of …/aidevops.sh)" ×40, "aidevops (basename of …/aidevops)" ×9). Each is a failed dispatch claim comment (`failed to post claim comment … after 3 attempt(s)`), which aborts the dispatch. The pulse dispatched 0–1 of 12–17 candidates per cycle, with 0 of 20 worker slots in use. Interactive PR creation is blocked the same way.

## Acceptance criteria

- A pulse-enabled repo with a public cache entry checked 1 hour ago is not in the private-slug list; one checked 8 days ago is.
- Cached-private and no-entry pulse repos are still enumerated.
- After deploy, `pulse.log` shows no new `[privacy-scan][BLOCK]` lines for known-public basenames, and dispatch claim comments post again.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh .agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`; `bash .agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard-shim.sh`; `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-public-privacy-guard.sh`
- Runtime: `privacy_enumerate_private_slugs` against the live config no longer lists the 14 expired-public slugs.

</details>

<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

</details>
